questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure DevOps project named Project1 and an Azure subscription named Sub1. Sub1 contains an Azure SQL database named DB1.  
  
You need to build a release pipeline that uses the Azure SQL Database Deployment task to update DB1.  
  
Which artifact type should you deploy?
questions.explanation:
The Azure SQL Database Deployment task (part of the Azure Pipelines tasks) deploys a DACPAC to update the schema of an Azure SQL Database. A DACPAC is a self-contained unit of SQL Server database schema deployment generated from a SQL Server Database Project or extracted via SqlPackage, and it is the artifact type the task expects for schema deployment. A BACPAC includes both schema and data and is used for database export/import or migration, not for this deployment task. MDF and LDF are raw physical database files (data and log files) that cannot be directly deployed via this pipeline task.

**Learn more:** [Azure SQL Database Deployment task - Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/reference/sql-azure-dacpac-deployment-v1)

questions.domain: Design and implement processes and communications
questions.question:
You have an app named App1 that you release by using Azure Pipelines. App1 has the versions shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783721886008-n0ksz2a4.png)  
  
You complete a code change to fix a bug that was introduced in version 3.4.3.  
  
Which version number should you assign to the release?
questions.explanation: Following semantic versioning, the current production release is 4.0.0. A bug fix release increments only the patch version (the third digit), resulting in 4.0.1. The version in which the bug was originally introduced (3.4.3) is irrelevant to determining the next version number from the current 4.0.0 release.

questions.domain: Implement an instrumentation strategy
questions.question:
You have a private distribution group that contains provisioned and unprovisioned devices.  

You need to distribute a new iOS application to the distribution group by using Microsoft Visual Studio App Center.  

What should you do?

options.text: Select Register devices and sign my app.
Create an active subscription in App Center Test.
Add the device owner to the organization in App Center.

questions.explanation: To distribute iOS applications to provisioned and unprovisioned devices in a private distribution group via App Center, devices must be registered and the app must be signed. Selecting 'Register devices and sign my app' enables auto-provisioning of devices and handles app signing for distribution.

questions.domain: Implement an instrumentation strategy
questions.question:
You have a project in Azure DevOps.  

You need to push notifications about pull requests to a Microsoft Teams channel. The solution must minimize development effort.  

What should you do?

options.text: Install the Azure Pipelines app for Teams and configure a subscription to receive notifications in the channel.
Use Azure Automation to connect to the Azure DevOps REST API and send messages to Teams.
Install the Azure Repos app for Teams and configure a subscription to receive notifications in the channel.
Use an Azure function to connect to the Azure DevOps REST API and send messages to Teams.

questions.explanation: The Azure Repos app for Teams is specifically designed for code-related notifications including pull requests, commits, and reviews. The Azure Pipelines app handles build and release events. For pull request notifications with minimal development effort, the Repos app is the correct choice.

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a multi-tier application consisting of an Azure Web Apps front end and an Azure SQL Database back end.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to capture and store telemetry data. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Support using ad-hoc queries to identify baselines.  
- Trigger alerts when metrics in the baseline are exceeded.  
- Store application and database metrics in a central location.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
A Log Analytics workspace centrally collects diagnostic logs and metrics from both the App Service front end and the Azure SQL Database back end. It supports Kusto Query Language for ad-hoc queries to establish performance baselines, and Azure Monitor alert rules can be created against the workspace data to notify when baseline thresholds are exceeded. This makes it the only option that satisfies all three stated requirements — centralized storage of multi-tier metrics, ad-hoc querying, and alerting on baseline deviations.

**Learn more:** [Monitor Azure SQL Database - Azure Monitor integration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/monitoring-sql-database-azure-monitor?view=azuresql) · [Configure Streaming Export of Metrics and Resource Logs - Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/metrics-diagnostic-telemetry-logging-streaming-export-configure?view=azuresql)

questions.domain: Design and implement processes and communications
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an Azure DevOps project, which includes a build pipeline that makes use of roughly fifty open source libraries.  

You have been tasked with making sure that you are able to scan project for common security weaknesses in the open source libraries.  

Which of the following actions should you take?

options.text: You should create a build task and use the WhiteSource Bolt service.
You should create a deployment task and use the WhiteSource Bolt service.
You should create a build task and use the Chef service.
You should create a deployment task and use the Chef service.

questions.explanation: Scanning for security vulnerabilities in open-source libraries should occur during the build phase, not deployment, to catch issues early in the development lifecycle. WhiteSource (now Mend) Bolt is specifically designed to scan for vulnerabilities and license compliance issues in open-source dependencies. Chef is a configuration management tool, not a security scanner.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
You are making use of Azure DevOps to configure Azure Pipelines for project, named PROJ-01.  

You are preparing to use a version control system that allows for source code to be stored on a managed Windows server located on the company network.  

Which of the following is the version control system you should use?
questions.explanation: GitHub Enterprise Server is the self-hosted edition of GitHub that an organization installs and runs on its own managed infrastructure inside its corporate network, matching the requirement to keep source code on a company-network server. Git in Azure Repos, by contrast, is a cloud-hosted Azure DevOps Services offering rather than software installed on a customer-managed Windows server.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains 50 virtual machines.  

You plan to manage the configuration of the virtual machines by using Azure Automation State Configuration.  

You need to create the Desired State Configuration (DSC) configuration files.  

How should you structure the code blocks?
questions.explanation: DSC uses a hierarchical structure: Configuration (defines the overall configuration), Node(s) (specify target systems), then Resource(s) (define desired states). This nesting allows a single configuration to target multiple nodes, each with potentially different resources configured.

questions.domain: Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains 50 virtual machines.  

You plan to manage the configuration of the virtual machines by using Azure Automation State Configuration.  

You need to create the Desired State Configuration (DSC) configuration files.  

How should you structure the code blocks?
questions.explanation:
Azure DevOps release pipelines let you configure, per stage, how queued deployments are processed via the Deployment queue settings. One of the available options, 'Deploy latest and cancel others,' automatically cancels or skips older queued releases and deploys only the most recent one when multiple releases are waiting for deployment to the same stage. This is exactly the mechanism designed to prevent outdated builds from being deployed after a newer build is already queued.

**Learn more:** [Release deployment control options - Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/release/deployment-queue-settings)

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure DevOps project that currently uses numerous package feeds.  
  
You need to simplify the project so that it relies on a single feed that:  
  
- Stores packages produced by your company  
- Stores packages consumed from remote feeds  
- Supports public feeds  
- Supports authenticated feeds  
  
What should you enable in DevOps?
questions.explanation:
Upstream sources in Azure Artifacts let a single feed serve as the one place developers get packages, whether those packages are published by your own team or retrieved from other locations such as public registries (nuget.org, npmjs.com, PyPI) or other authenticated Azure DevOps/Artifactory feeds. When a package is requested that isn't already in the feed, Azure Artifacts automatically saves a copy from the configured upstream source, consolidating package management into one feed while still supporting both public and authenticated remote sources.

**Learn more:** [Use upstream sources - Azure Artifacts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/artifacts/concepts/upstream-sources)

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
Solution: You recommend increasing test coverage.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation: Greater test coverage can make future changes safer and help avoid additional debt, but it does not itself remove the existing technical debt that delays feature development. Existing debt must be addressed directly, such as through refactoring or remediation work.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
Solution: You propose reducing code complexity.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation: Lower code complexity improves maintainability and reduces the effort and risk involved in changing, testing, and extending software, thereby helping reduce accumulated technical debt.

questions.domain: Design and implement processes and communications
questions.question:
Solution: You recommend increasing code duplication.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation: Code duplication increases maintenance effort and inconsistency risk because equivalent logic must be maintained in multiple locations. Reducing duplication is a common way to reduce technical debt and speed future feature development.

questions.domain: Design and implement processes and communications
questions.question:
Solution: You recommend decreasing code coupling and dependency cycles.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation: Reducing code coupling and eliminating dependency cycles makes components more independent, easier to change, test, and maintain. This reduces accumulated technical debt and helps shorten the time needed to add application features.

questions.domain: Design and implement processes and communications
questions.question:
You are currently defining a release strategy for an app, named APP-01.  

The strategy should allow you to keep the time it takes to deploy new releases of the app to a minimum. The strategy should also allow you to roll back in the shortest time required.  

Which of the following is the release strategy you should use?
questions.explanation: Red/Black deployment (also known as Blue/Green) maintains two identical production environments. New releases deploy to the inactive environment, then traffic switches instantly once verified. This approach minimizes deployment time and enables immediate rollback by switching traffic back—no gradual transitions or downtime required. Rolling deployment requires gradual updates; Canary deployment is slower for rollback; Big Bang is high-risk.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],To resolve the current technical issue, what should you do to the Register-AzureRmAutomationDscNode command?

options.text: Change the value of the ConfigurationMode parameter.

questions.explanation:
The Register-AzureRmAutomationDscNode cmdlet's ConfigurationMode parameter determines how Azure Automation State Configuration (DSC) applies and maintains a node's configuration. Setting it to ApplyOnly causes DSC to apply the configuration a single time and never check for or correct drift afterward, which is why previously correctly configured servers were drifting out of compliance over time. Changing the ConfigurationMode value to ApplyAndAutoCorrect causes DSC to periodically check the node against the desired configuration and automatically correct any detected drift, resolving the issue.

**Learn more:** [To resolve the current technical issue, what should you do to the Register-AzureRmAutomationDscNode command? - Exam4Training](https://www.exam4training.com/to-resolve-the-current-technical-issue-what-should-you-do-to-the-register-azurermautomationdscnode-command-11/)

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783721759755-rd2p7edp.png)  
  
DepPipeline1 and ADFPipeline1 use a single credential that is stored in Vault1.  
  
You need to configure ADFPipeline1 to retrieve the credential from Vault1.  
  
Which type of activity should you use?
questions.explanation: The Web activity in Azure Data Factory is designed to make HTTP requests to external endpoints, including Azure Key Vault. By configuring a Web activity to query the Key Vault REST API, you can retrieve secrets and store them for use by other pipeline activities. Lookup, Get Metadata, and Copy activities serve different purposes in data movement and retrieval but are not designed for credential retrieval.

questions.domain: Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.question:
You have an Azure web app named webapp1 that uses the .NET Core runtime stack. You have an Azure Application Insights resource named AppInsights1. Webapp1 sends telemetry data to AppInsights1.  
  
You need to ensure that webapp1 sends the telemetry data at a fixed sampling rate.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the code repository of webapp1, modify the ApplicationInsights.config file.
From the code repository of webapp1, modify the Startup.cs file.
From AppInsights1, modify the Usage and estimated costs settings.
From AppInsights1, configure the Continuous export settings.

questions.explanation: .NET Core applications use the Startup.cs file (or Program.cs in newer versions) to configure Application Insights sampling. ApplicationInsights.config is specific to .NET Framework and does not apply to .NET Core. Settings in Azure Portal affect the entire resource, not app-specific sampling rates.

questions.domain: Design and implement processes and communications
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a build pipeline in Azure Pipelines that uses separate jobs to compile an application for 10 different architectures. The build pipeline currently takes approximately one day to complete.  
  
You need to reduce the time it takes to run the build pipeline.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
*(Choose two.)*

options.text: Move to a blue/green deployment pattern
Increase the number of parallel jobs
Reduce the size of the repository

questions.explanation: To reduce a 10-architecture parallel build pipeline from one day: (C) increasing the number of parallel jobs allows more of the 10 independent architecture jobs to run concurrently instead of queuing, and (E) creating an agent pool provides the compute capacity to support that parallelism. Together these directly reduce total pipeline duration by running jobs simultaneously. Reducing repository size (D) helps but is a secondary optimization; deploying and managing groups (A, B) are unrelated to build compilation speed.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have set up an Azure DevOps project for a new application that will be deployed across several Windows Server 2016 Azure virtual machines.  
  
You need to design a deployment solution that:  
  
- Ensures the virtual machines maintain a uniform configuration  
- Keeps the administrative effort required to configure the virtual machines to a minimum  
  
Which two of the following should be part of your solution? (Choose two.)

options.text: The PowerShell Desired State Configuration (DSC) extension for Windows
The Custom Script Extension for Windows

questions.explanation:
ARM templates provide a declarative, idempotent way to provision the virtual machines so every instance is created with the same baseline configuration, eliminating manual setup steps. The PowerShell DSC extension for Windows then applies and continuously enforces a desired configuration state on each VM, automatically remediating any configuration drift, which keeps the machines uniform over time with minimal ongoing administrative effort. Together these two technologies handle both initial provisioning consistency and ongoing configuration management, whereas the Custom Script Extension only executes a script once and does not maintain state, and deployment groups/pipeline stage templates are release orchestration constructs rather than configuration management tools.

**Learn more:** [Azure Automation State Configuration (DSC) overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/automation/automation-dsc-overview) · [DSC extension handler for Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/extensions/dsc-overview)

questions.domain: Implement an instrumentation strategy
questions.question:
Solution: Set the `-ConfigurationMode` parameter to `ApplyAndMonitor`.  
  
Does this solution satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
`ApplyAndMonitor` applies an initial configuration and reports subsequent configuration drift, but it does not automatically correct that drift. Servers remain noncompliant until they are manually remediated unless the configuration mode is `ApplyAndAutoCorrect`.\
\
**Learn more:** [Remediate noncompliant Azure Automation State Configuration servers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/automation/automation-dsc-remediate) · [Register-AzAutomationDscNode (Az.Automation)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.automation/register-azautomationdscnode)

questions.domain: Design and implement processes and communications
questions.question:
Solution: You configure the `-ConfigurationMode` parameter as `ApplyAndAutocorrect`.  
  
Does this solution achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
`ApplyAndAutocorrect` automatically reapplies the desired DSC configuration when a node drifts from its compliant state, thereby remediating drift and keeping servers correctly configured.\
\
**Learn more:** [Remediate noncompliant Azure Automation State Configuration servers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/automation/automation-dsc-remediate) · [Register-AzAutomationDscNode (Az.Automation)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.automation/register-azautomationdscnode)

questions.question:
Solution: Set the `-ConfigurationMode` parameter to `ApplyOnly`.  
  
Does this solution achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
`ApplyOnly` applies the configuration initially but does not subsequently check for or remediate configuration drift. Maintaining the required configuration despite drift requires `ApplyAndAutoCorrect`.\
\
**Learn more:** [Remediate noncompliant Azure Automation State Configuration servers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/automation/automation-dsc-remediate) · [Configure machines to a desired state in Azure Automation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/automation/tutorial-configure-servers-desired-state)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are configuring an alert rule in Azure Monitor for the ASP-9bb7 resource, as shown in the exhibit below.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783719579988-bthtqarc.jpg)  
  
Which action will cause this alert to fire?

options.text: a failed attempt to delete the ASP-9bb7 resource
a change to a role assignment for the ASP-9bb7 resource
a successful attempt to delete the ASP-9bb7 resource
a failed attempt to scale up the ASP-9bb7 resource

questions.explanation:
The alert rule's condition is: Activity Log, Category='Administrative', Signal name='All Administrative operations', Status='failed'. The Administrative category in the Azure Activity Log records create, update, delete, and action operations performed through Azure Resource Manager, and both the start and the success/fail outcome of each such operation are logged. Because the rule's Status filter is set specifically to 'failed', only a failed administrative operation on ASP-9bb7 (such as a failed delete) satisfies the condition. A successful delete has Status='Succeeded' and does not match. Scale operations (whether manual or via autoscale) are logged under the distinct 'Autoscale' Activity Log category, not 'Administrative', so a failed scale-up attempt would not be captured by this rule. A role-assignment change is logged under Administrative but is not stated to have failed, so it does not reliably satisfy the Status='failed' requirement the way an explicitly failed delete attempt does.

**Learn more:** [Activity Log in Azure Monitor - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/platform/activity-log) · [Azure Activity Log event schema - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/platform/activity-log-schema)

questions.domain: Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company follows an Agile development approach and you are planning to hold retrospectives at the end of each sprint.  
  
Which three questions should be included in the retrospective? Each correct answer presents part of the solution. (Choose three.)  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A sprint retrospective is a team-focused meeting used to inspect how the last sprint went in terms of people, relationships, processes, and tools, and to identify improvements. The standard set of retrospective questions asks: What went well?, What could have gone better?, and What should we try next (or do differently)? These questions keep the focus on the team's process and outcomes rather than singling out individual team members' performance, which is why questions about who performed well or should have performed better are not part of a proper retrospective format.

**Learn more:** [Sprint and scrum best practices - Azure Boards | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/boards/sprints/best-practices-scrum?view=azure-devops) · [Retrospectives: The Hidden Gem Enabling Teams to Thrive - Part 1 - Azure DevOps Blog](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/devops/retrospectives-the-hidden-gem-enabling-teams-to-thrive-part-1/)

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.explanation: "Automatically watch teams" is what silently subscribes you to every team's discussions the moment you join it, and "Watching" is the delivery setting that emails you about everything you are subscribed to, including those auto-watched teams; clearing both stops the blanket team-discussion emails. Leaving "Participating and @mentions" selected keeps the emails you actually want, and "Automatically watch repositories" is unrelated because it governs repositories, not team discussions.

questions.question:
You use Calendar Versioning (CalVer) for code assets.  
  
You need to store an optional tag of beta as part of the version.  
  
Which part of the version should you use for the tag?
questions.explanation: In Calendar Versioning (CalVer), the modifier segment holds optional text tags such as 'alpha', 'beta', 'rc', or 'dev' to indicate pre-release status. The full format is MAJOR.MINOR.MICRO-MODIFIER (e.g., 2024.07.15-beta). The modifier is distinct from major, minor, and micro version components.

questions.explanation: Pester is the dedicated testing framework for PowerShell, specifically designed for writing unit and integration tests for PowerShell scripts and Desired State Configuration (DSC). It integrates directly into CI/CD pipelines and provides comprehensive testing capabilities to validate DSC configurations before deployment. PSScriptAnalyzer, PSCodeHealth, and Test-DscConfiguration serve different purposes (code analysis, health monitoring, and verification respectively) but are not comprehensive testing frameworks.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
You have a pipeline named Pipeline1 in Azure Pipelines.  
  
You need to create a service connection to enable Pipeline1 to download a public container image.  
  
Which type of service connection should you create?
questions.explanation: A Docker registry service connection enables pipelines to authenticate with and pull container images from registries (Docker Hub, Azure Container Registry, etc.). This is distinct from a Docker host connection, which manages remote Docker daemon access for running containers.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
You have a project in Azure DevOps.  

You plan to deploy a self-hosted agent by using an unattended configuration script.  

Which two values should you define in the configuration script? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation: For unattended self-hosted agent configuration, you must specify the organization URL (where the agent registers) and authorization credentials (PAT, username/password, or Windows Auth). Other values like project name and pool name are optional or can be set interactively.

questions.question:
You manage code by using GitHub.  
  
You plan to ensure that all GitHub Actions are validated by a security team.  
  
You create a branch protection rule requiring that code changes be reviewed by code owners.  
  
You need to create the CODEOWNERS file.  
  
Where should you create the file?
questions.explanation: GitHub's CODEOWNERS file designates code ownership and can be placed in the repository root, docs/, or .github/ directory. The .github/ directory is a standard location for GitHub configuration files and is a valid choice for the CODEOWNERS file.

options.text: Add a Parent link to the user story of itemA.
From Backlogs, open the context menu, select Add link, and then select itemA. Set Link type to Successor and add the ID of itemB.
From Backlogs, open the context menu, select Add link, and then select itemB. Set Link type to Related and add the ID of itemA.
From itemA, open the Links tab, and then select Add link. Set Link type to References and add the ID of itemB.

questions.explanation: From the Backlogs view, you can right-click a work item to open its context menu, choose Add link, pick the related item, and set the Link type to Successor/Predecessor to record that one item cannot proceed until the other completes, capturing the dependency directly from the backlog with minimal navigation. A Parent link only expresses hierarchy, and Related/References links carry no ordering semantics, so they don't model a true dependency.

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains an Azure Pipelines pipeline named Pipeline1 and an app named App1. Pipeline1 is used to automate the building of App1.  
  
You have a Slack channel named App1chat that includes an incoming webhook.  
  
You need to ensure that when a successful build of App1 is created, a notification is sent to App1chat by using the webhook.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation: A service hook subscription in Azure DevOps is used to connect build/release events to external services like Slack using webhooks. This is the standard mechanism for sending build notifications to external systems. Notifications are for internal alerts, alert rules and action groups are Azure Monitor constructs, not DevOps integration points.

questions.domain: Design and implement processes and communications
questions.question:
You have an Azure Automation account that contains a runbook. The runbook is used to configure the application infrastructure of an Azure subscription.  
  
You have a project in Azure DevOps named Project1. Project1 contains a repository that stores code for the runbook.  
  
You need to ensure that every committed change to the code will update automatically and publish the runbook to Azure Automation.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: the Service hooks settings for Project1
the Connections settings for the Automation account
the Source control settings for the Automation account
the Service connections settings for Project1

questions.explanation: Azure Automation's Source Control integration enables automatic synchronization and publishing of runbooks from an Azure DevOps repository. Configuring source control settings establishes this connection, allowing committed changes to trigger automatic runbook updates.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a project hosted in Azure DevOps. Within Visual Studio, you have an Azure Resource Group deployment project that has been checked in to that Azure DevOps project.  
  
You need to create a release pipeline that will deploy resources using Azure Resource Manager templates. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
Which task type should you include in the solution?
questions.explanation:
A Visual Studio Azure Resource Group deployment project automatically includes a Deploy-AzureResourceGroup.ps1 PowerShell script (along with the ARM template and parameters files) that already contains the logic to deploy the template to a resource group using cmdlets such as New-AzResourceGroupDeployment. Because this script is already checked into source control as part of the project, the release pipeline only needs an Azure PowerShell task configured to run that existing script file against the target Azure subscription — no custom deployment logic or additional resource-specific tasks need to be built, which minimizes administrative effort. The other task types (Cloud Service Deployment, RM Web App Deployment, App Service Manage) are designed for different resource types and don't natively consume this generated deployment script.

**Learn more:** [Create & deploy Visual Studio resource group projects - Azure Resource Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/templates/create-visual-studio-deployment-project) · [AzurePowerShell@5 - Azure PowerShell v5 task](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/reference/azure-powershell-v5?view=azure-pipelines)

You are making use of Azure DevOps manage build pipelines, and also deploy pipelines.  

The development team is quite large, and is regularly added to.  

You have been informed that the management of users and licenses must be automated when it can be.  

Which of the following is a task that can't be automated?
questions.explanation: License procurement—the purchasing of licenses from vendors—requires manual business processes including vendor negotiations, contract reviews, and purchasing approval. It cannot be automated. In contrast, group membership changes, license assignment to users, and entitlement provisioning can all be automated through Azure Active Directory and Azure DevOps automation tools.

Add GH-123 to the text of the commit message.
From the Links settings of work item 123, select Add link, select Existing item, and then enter the URL of the commit.
To work item 123, add a comment that includes the URL of the commit.

questions.explanation:
Typing AB#123 in a GitHub commit or pull request message automatically links that commit to Azure Boards work item 123. You can also open work item 123, expand its Development section, choose Add link, and paste the commit's URL directly; the Links tab's "Add link > Existing item" flow is meant for relating one Azure Boards work item to another, not for attaching external GitHub commit URLs.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are planning to consume a NuGet package within a project hosted in Azure DevOps. This NuGet package resides in a feed that requires authentication.  
  
You need to make sure the project can restore the NuGet package automatically.  
  
What should the project use to automate the authentication process?

options.text: an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) account that has multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled
an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) service principal

questions.explanation:
The Azure Artifacts Credential Provider automates the process of acquiring credentials needed for NuGet client tools (such as dotnet, nuget.exe, and MSBuild) to authenticate to Azure Artifacts feeds. It handles authentication transparently so that package restore operations can complete automatically without requiring interactive sign-in, making it the correct mechanism for automating NuGet package restore from an authenticated feed in Azure DevOps.

**Learn more:** [Azure Artifacts Credential Provider](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/artifacts/nuget/nuget-exe?view=azure-devops#the-azure-artifacts-credential-provider)

questions.question:
You have an app named App1 that uses Application Insights to monitor application performance.  
  
You need to analyze how often a page in App1 is accessed.  
  
Which pane in Application Insights should you use?
questions.explanation: The Events pane in Application Insights tracks how often specific pages and features are used. Page views are recorded when a page is loaded, making Events the appropriate tool to analyze access frequency. Sessions (B) tracks user sessions, Impact (C) measures feature dependency, and Users (D) shows user counts—none directly measure access frequency.

You have an Azure DevOps organization named Contoso.  

You need to receive Microsoft Teams notifications when work items are updated.  

What should you do?

options.text: From Azure DevOps, configure a service hook subscription
From Microsoft Teams, configure a connector
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, configure external access
From Microsoft Teams, add a channel
From Azure DevOps, install an extension

questions.explanation: Notification integration between Azure DevOps and Microsoft Teams for work item events is set up by first configuring a connector inside the target Microsoft Teams channel; attempting to create the subscription directly from Azure DevOps redirects you to Teams, since ownership of that subscription lives with the consuming (Teams) service.

questions.domain: Implement an instrumentation strategy
questions.question:
You have an Azure DevOps organization named Contoso.  

You need to receive Microsoft Teams notifications when work items are updated.  

What should you do?

options.text: Create an Azure logic app that has an HTTP request trigger.
Create an Azure logic app that has an Azure DevOps trigger.
Modify an action group in Azure Monitor.
Modify the Diagnostics settings in Azure Monitor.

questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor action groups do not natively support posting to Microsoft Teams, so a Logic App must be used as an intermediary. The Logic App needs an HTTP request trigger so that Azure Monitor's action group can invoke it as a webhook when the alert fires; the Logic App workflow then uses the Microsoft Teams connector to post the alert message to a channel. To connect this new capability into the existing alerting setup, the existing action group must be modified to add an action (Logic App/webhook) that calls the Logic App's HTTP endpoint whenever the alert condition is met. An Azure DevOps-triggered Logic App would not respond to Azure Monitor alerts, a workbook only visualizes data, and diagnostic settings route logs/metrics rather than trigger notification actions.

**Learn more:** [Customize alert notifications by using Logic Apps - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-logic-apps) · [Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups)

questions.domain: Implement an instrumentation strategy
questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor Workbooks let you combine markdown text, parameters, and visualizations driven by Kusto Query Language (KQL) queries into a single interactive report. Access to workbooks is governed by Azure RBAC using Azure AD identities, and because workbooks query data live each time they are opened, the visuals always reflect the most current data. This combination of RBAC support, KQL-based visuals, markdown documentation, and live data satisfies all the stated requirements, which the other options (Power BI, Azure Data Explorer alone, or Azure dashboards) do not fully provide.

**Learn more:** [Azure Monitor Workbooks overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/visualize/workbooks-overview)

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an existing project in Azure DevOps. You are planning to integrate GitHub as the repository for this project. You need to ensure that Azure Pipelines runs under the Azure Pipelines identity.  
  
Which authentication mechanism should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Azure Pipelines GitHub App is the recommended authentication mechanism for connecting Azure Pipelines to GitHub repositories. Once installed in the GitHub account or organization, it becomes the default authentication method for pipelines and causes builds and GitHub status updates to run under the dedicated Azure Pipelines service identity, rather than under the personal identity of the user who set up the connection. In contrast, both OAuth and personal access token (PAT) authentication tie the pipeline to the individual user's GitHub identity, meaning the pipeline could break if that user's access changes or is revoked. Azure AD is not applicable for this GitHub integration scenario. This makes the GitHub App the correct choice for ensuring pipeline runs use the Azure Pipelines identity.

**Learn more:** [Build GitHub repositories - Azure Pipelines | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/repos/github?view=azure-devops)

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company deploys applications using Docker containers. You want to detect known exploits in the Docker images used to provision the Docker containers. You need to integrate image scanning into the application lifecycle, and the solution must expose the exploits as early as possible during the application lifecycle.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: a task executed in the continuous integration pipeline and a scheduled task that analyzes the image registry
manual tasks performed during the planning phase and the deployment phase
a task executed in the continuous deployment pipeline and a scheduled task against a running production container
a task executed in the continuous integration pipeline and a scheduled task that analyzes the production container

questions.explanation:
Scanning images as part of the continuous integration pipeline detects known vulnerabilities at build time, which is the earliest possible point in the application lifecycle — before an image is ever pushed or deployed. Because new CVEs are discovered continuously after images are built, a scheduled task that re-analyzes the image registry ensures that images already stored (and possibly deployed) are re-evaluated against newly published vulnerability data, so exploits discovered after the initial CI scan are still detected. This combination (CI-time scanning plus ongoing registry scanning) provides both early detection and continuous coverage, which is the approach used by services such as Google Container Registry/Artifact Registry vulnerability scanning via the Container Analysis API.

**Learn more:** [Container Analysis - Scanning images for vulnerabilities](https://cloud.google.com/container-analysis/docs/container-scanning-overview)

In GitHub Actions workflow trigger filters, glob patterns use double-asterisk (**) to match across directory levels, while single-asterisk (*) only matches within a single path segment. To trigger on pull requests to branches prefixed with 'releases/', the pattern 'releases/**' is required because it matches any branch name that begins with that prefix regardless of additional path segments (e.g., releases/2023, releases/2023/hotfix). For the paths filter, scanning all files within subdirectories of src requires 'src/**', since 'src/*' only matches files directly inside src and not nested subdirectories. For paths-ignore, excluding all markdown files anywhere in the repository (not just at the root) requires '**/*.md', because '*.md' only matches markdown files in the root directory. These glob semantics are documented in GitHub's workflow syntax reference for filtering branches and paths.

Your company has an Azure DevOps project. The source code for the project is stored in an on-premises repository and uses an on-premises build server.  
  
You plan to use Azure DevOps to control the build process on the build server by using a self-hosted agent.  
  
You need to implement the self-hosted agent. You download and install the agent on the build server.  
  
Which two actions should you perform next? (Each correct answer presents part of the solution.)

options.text: From Azure, create a shared access signature (SAS).
From the build server, create a certificate, and then upload the certificate to Azure Storage.
From the build server, create a certificate, and then upload the certificate to Azure Key Vault.
From DevOps, create a personal access token (PAT).
From the build server, run config.cmd.

questions.explanation:
After downloading and installing a self-hosted agent, you must authenticate it to your Azure DevOps organization and then configure it. Azure DevOps uses a Personal Access Token (PAT) as the standard authentication mechanism for self-hosted agents to register with the service — you generate the PAT from Azure DevOps and supply it during agent configuration. Configuration itself is performed by running config.cmd (on Windows) or config.sh (on Linux/macOS) from the agent's installation directory on the build server; this script prompts for the organization URL, the authentication type (PAT), the PAT value, agent pool, and agent name, and registers the agent with Azure DevOps. Certificates uploaded to Azure Storage or Key Vault, and SAS tokens, are not part of the self-hosted agent registration process.

**Learn more:** [Self-hosted Windows agents - Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/agents/v2-windows?view=azure-devops) · [Use personal access tokens - Azure DevOps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/organizations/accounts/use-personal-access-tokens-to-authenticate?view=azure-devops)

questions.question:
You need to consider the underlined segment to establish whether it is accurate.  

When moving to Azure DevOps, JIRA must be replaced with the build pipelines Azure DevOps service.  

Select `No adjustment required` if the underlined segment is accurate. If the underlined segment is inaccurate, select the accurate option.
questions.explanation: JIRA is a task and project management tool, not a build pipeline tool. When migrating to Azure DevOps, JIRA should be replaced with Azure Boards, which provides equivalent agile project management and work item tracking capabilities.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
Solution: On the build pipeline’s **Triggers** tab, you select **Enable continuous integration**.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
An enabled continuous-integration trigger automatically queues a build whenever code is checked in to a branch covered by the trigger.\
\
**Learn more:** [Build Azure Repos Git repositories - Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/repos/azure-repos-git?view=azure-devops) · [Specify events that trigger pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/build/triggers?view=azure-devops)

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
Solution: In the release pipeline’s **Pre-deployment conditions** settings, select **Batch changes while a build is in progress**.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Automatic builds on code check-in require a continuous integration (CI) trigger on the build pipeline. Release-pipeline pre-deployment conditions control release-stage deployment behavior; they do not configure a build to start when source code is checked in. Azure Pipelines documentation distinguishes CI triggers, which run pipelines on pushes, from continuous-deployment triggers, which start classic releases after builds complete.\
\
**Learn more:** [Triggers in Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/build/triggers?view=azure-devops) · [Classic release triggers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/release/triggers?view=azure-devops-2022)

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
Solution: In the Continuous deployment trigger settings for the release pipeline, enable the **Pull request trigger** setting.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation: A release pipeline pull request trigger does not cause a build to run whenever code is checked in. Automatically building on check-in requires a continuous integration trigger configured on the build pipeline.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
Solution: You deploy a Docker build to an on-premises server and add a Download Build Artifacts task to the deployment pipeline.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Download Build Artifacts task downloads files saved as artifacts from a completed build to the agent or deployment target. It does not deploy or run a Docker image; a Docker deployment requires an additional mechanism to make the image available and run it on the on-premises server.\
\
**Learn more:** [DownloadBuildArtifacts@0 - Download build artifacts v0 task](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/reference/download-build-artifacts-v0?view=azure-pipelines)

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
Solution: Deploy an Azure self-hosted agent to an on-premises server, and add a Copy and Publish Build Artifacts task to the deployment pipeline.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
A self-hosted agent executes pipeline tasks on its on-premises host. The Copy and Publish Build Artifacts task can copy build outputs to a file share that is accessible from the build agent, enabling artifacts to be placed in the on-premises environment.\
\
**Learn more:** [CopyPublishBuildArtifacts@1 - Copy and Publish Build Artifacts v1 task](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/reference/copy-publish-build-artifacts-v1?view=azure-pipelines) · [Azure Pipelines agents](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/agents/agents?view=azure-devops)

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
Solution: You deploy an on-premises Kubernetes cluster. You deploy a Helm agent to that cluster. You add a Download Build Artifacts task to the deployment pipeline.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Download Build Artifacts downloads files saved from a completed build; it does not deploy them to Kubernetes. A deployment requires an execution step, such as a Helm deployment command or task, to install or upgrade the workload in the cluster.\
\
**Learn more:** [DownloadBuildArtifacts@0 - Download build artifacts v0 task](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/reference/download-build-artifacts-v0?view=azure-pipelines)

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
Solution: Add a code-coverage step to the build pipelines.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
A code-coverage build step collects test-coverage information; it does not control who can modify Azure DevOps project configuration. Project-level permissions govern changes to project information, properties, and related configuration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Permissions, security groups, and service accounts reference - Azure DevOps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/organizations/security/permissions?view=azure-devops)

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
Solution: Add a code-coverage step to the build pipelines.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
A continuous integration trigger is required to run a build when code is pushed or checked in. The **After stage** pre-deployment trigger controls progression between stages in a classic release pipeline after a selected stage deploys successfully; it does not trigger a build from a code check-in. [Triggers in Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/build/triggers?view=azure-devops), [Classic release triggers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/release/triggers?view=azure-devops-2022)

**Learn more:** [Triggers in Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/build/triggers?view=azure-devops) · [Classic release triggers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/release/triggers?view=azure-devops-2022)

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
Solution: Implement Continuous Integration for the project.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation: Continuous Integration automates the build and validation of integrated code changes; it does not prevent changes to an Azure DevOps project's configuration over time.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
Solution: Implement Continuous Assurance for the project.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation: Continuous Assurance repeatedly checks a project’s configuration against its approved baseline to detect configuration drift, helping maintain the required configuration state over time.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
Solution: You deploy an Octopus Deploy server. You install a polling Tentacle agent on an on-premises server. You add an Octopus task to the deployment pipeline.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Octopus Deploy uses Tentacle as an agent on deployment targets to deploy packages and run deployment tasks. A polling Tentacle retrieves work from the Octopus Server, which supports deployments to an on-premises server while accommodating networks that do not allow inbound connectivity to that server.\
\
**Learn more:** [Octopus Tentacle documentation](https://octopus.com/docs/infrastructure/deployment-targets/tentacle)

options.text: an Azure Load Balancer health probe

questions.explanation:
Azure Container Instances supports readiness probes, which determine whether a container is ready to accept incoming traffic. Until the readiness probe succeeds, the container is not considered available to serve requests, which is exactly what's needed to ensure DB1 has finished loading its startup data before App1 begins accepting user requests. A liveness probe only checks whether a running container should be restarted due to an unresponsive state and does not gate initial readiness; performance logs provide diagnostic data rather than traffic control; and Azure Load Balancer health probes apply to load balancer backend pools, not to container groups in Azure Container Instances.

**Learn more:** [Azure Container Instances - add liveness and readiness probes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-instances/container-instances-liveness-probe)

Solution: You include the following elements in the pipeline’s YAML definition.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785752203983-2blzw6ge.png)  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Pipelines stages run sequentially by default, meaning a stage without an explicit dependency depends on the immediately preceding stage. `Publish_Test_Results` therefore does not wait for both test stages; it needs `dependsOn` for both `Test_App` and `Test_Database`. It also lacks `condition: always()`, so it is not guaranteed to run when a dependency fails.\
\
**Learn more:** [Stages in Azure Pipelines YAML schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/yaml-schema/stages-stage?view=azure-pipelines) · [Pipeline conditions in Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/process/conditions?view=azure-devops)

questions.question:
Solution: You include the following elements in the pipeline’s YAML definition.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785752203983-2blzw6ge.png)  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
In Azure Pipelines, `dependsOn: []` explicitly removes a stage's dependency on the preceding stage. Therefore, `Test_App` and `Test_Database` can run in parallel, but they can start without waiting for `Build_App` to complete successfully. This violates the requirement that both test stages run only after a successful build. The results stage does wait for the listed stages and `succeededOrFailed()` allows it to run after dependency failures, but the missing build-to-test dependency means the overall design does not satisfy the requirements.

**Learn more:** [stages.stage definition - Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/yaml-schema/stages-stage?view=azure-pipelines) · [Pipeline conditions - Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/process/conditions?view=azure-devops)

`Test_App` and `Test_Database` both depend only on `Build_App`, so they can run concurrently after the build succeeds. `Publish_Test_Results` depends on both test stages, ensuring that it starts only after they complete, and `condition: always()` makes it run regardless of their outcome. questions.question:
You manage code by using GitHub.  
  
You plan to use Dependabot to scan for code dependencies.  
  
You need to identify when scanning will be triggered automatically.  
  
Which two actions will trigger a scan? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct solution is worth one point.

options.text: The dependency graph of a repository changes.

questions.explanation: Dependabot automatically scans when the dependency graph changes (such as adding or updating dependencies), and when a new advisory is added to the GitHub Advisory Database. These two events trigger Dependabot to check for vulnerable dependencies and notify the repository. Pull requests, branch forks, and commits do not automatically trigger scans.

questions.question:
Your company is building a new solution in Java.  

The company currently uses a SonarQube server to analyze the code of .NET solutions.  

You need to analyze and monitor the code quality of the Java solution.  

Which task types should you add to the build pipeline?
questions.explanation: Gradle is the JVM build tool used for Java projects, and its SonarQube plugin integrates directly into the Gradle build to run static analysis as part of the pipeline. Octopus is a deployment/release tool, Chef is a configuration-management tool, and CocoaPods is an iOS/Swift dependency manager, none of which build or analyze Java code.

questions.question:
You are designing a YAML template for use with Azure Pipelines. The template will include the outputfile parameter.  

Which two methods can you use to reference the parameter? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation: Template expressions in Azure Pipelines use double-brace syntax (${{ }}). Both property dereference syntax (${{parameters.outputfile}}) and index syntax (${{parameters['outputfile']}}) are valid for referencing parameters. Single-brace syntax ($(variable)) is for runtime/macro expansion, not template parameters.

questions.question:
You use an Azure Pipelines pipeline to build, test, and deploy an app named App1.  
  
You need to reduce how long it takes to complete unit and integration tests for App1. The solution must ensure that the code coverage testing ratio is maintained.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation: Test Impact Analysis (TIA) intelligently selects only the subset of tests affected by code changes, reducing execution time while maintaining coverage. This avoids running unnecessary tests on unchanged code. Flaky test management doesn't speed up tests, purchasing parallel jobs is costly, and additional agents don't inherently reduce test duration per se.

questions.question:
You have a project in Azure DevOps named Project1.  
  
You need to ensure that all new pipelines in Project1 execute three specific tasks during pipeline execution.  
  
What should you create?
questions.explanation: YAML templates are the modern approach for defining reusable pipeline logic in Azure DevOps. They allow you to define specific tasks once and reference them across multiple pipelines, ensuring consistency and reducing maintenance effort. Task groups serve a similar purpose but are associated with classic pipelines, making YAML templates the preferred solution for current Azure DevOps practices.

You have a project in Azure DevOps named Project1 that contains a Kanban board named Board1.  
  
You create a Microsoft Teams channel and add the Azure Boards app to the channel.  
  
You need to ensure that users can create work items in Board1 from Microsoft Teams.  
  
Which command should you run?
questions.explanation: To link an Azure Boards project from Microsoft Teams, the first step is to run '@azure boards link' with the project URL. This establishes the connection and enables subsequent work item creation via '@azure boards create'. The link command must precede any work item operations.

You have a project in Azure DevOps that has a release pipeline.  

You need to integrate work item tracking and an Agile project management system to meet the following requirements:  

✑ Ensure that developers can track whether their commits are deployed to production.  

✑ Report the deployment status.  

✑ Minimize integration effort.  

Which system should you use?
questions.explanation: Jira is a mature agile project management platform that integrates with Azure DevOps. It provides work item tracking, agile boards, release tracking, and deployment status reporting. Other tools (Asana, Basecamp, Trello) do not integrate as deeply with Azure DevOps pipelines.

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains a storage account and 20 virtual machines.  
  
You plan to use LogRhythm for aggregation and analysis of the virtual machine logs.  
  
You need to configure AzLog to export the logs and push them to the storage account.  
  
In which format should you export the logs?
questions.explanation: The LogRhythm Open Collector accepts logs in JSON format for modern cloud sources. JSON is the standard structured format for integrating cloud logs into LogRhythm SIEM. EVTX and EVT are Windows event log formats not suitable for cloud log ingestion; binary is also not a standard format for this purpose.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization is worried that when developers add open source libraries to a project, it can introduce licensing compliance problems.  
  
You need to add an automated step to the build pipeline that detects when common open source libraries are added to the codebase.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
WhiteSource Bolt is a software composition analysis (SCA) tool designed to integrate directly into build pipelines (such as Azure DevOps or Jenkins) to automatically scan a codebase, identify open source components and libraries in use, and flag their associated licenses so that licensing compliance issues can be detected early in the development process. OWASP ZAP is a dynamic application security testing (DAST) tool focused on finding runtime web vulnerabilities, not license or dependency detection. Jenkins is a general-purpose CI/CD automation server and does not itself perform open source library or license detection. Code Style tools enforce coding conventions and formatting, unrelated to license compliance scanning.

**Learn more:** [WhiteSource Bolt overview](https://docs.mend.io/bundle/wsbolt/page/getting_started_with_whitesource_bolt.html)

options.text: Microsoft Visual Studio App Center integration

questions.explanation:
Visual Studio App Center provides an end-to-end mobile DevOps solution that integrates with Azure DevOps pipelines. It offers Diagnostics for automatic crash and error reporting, Distribute for delivering beta builds to testers across Android and iOS, and in-app feedback/beta tester feedback capabilities to gather input on new app functionality. This combination directly satisfies all three requirements, which is not covered by the Test & Feedback extension (designed for exploratory testing by internal teams, not mobile beta distribution), Application Insights (primarily for web/service telemetry), or Jenkins integration (a CI/CD tool unrelated to mobile crash reporting and beta distribution).

questions.explanation:
Kanban boards in Azure DevOps are specifically designed to visualize the flow of work items through customizable columns representing different stages of a workflow, which aligns with the Kanban agile methodology's core principle of visualizing work in progress. This differs from sprint planning (organizing work into time-boxed iterations), delivery plans (calendar-based cross-team scheduling view), and portfolio backlogs (hierarchical grouping of work items across backlog levels), none of which are primarily focused on visualizing workflow.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to create a GitHub workflow that will use GitHub Actions. The actions will require a 256-KB secret.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to store and encrypt the secret. The secret value must be accessible only to the workflow. The solution must minimize administrative effort  
  
What should you recommend?

options.text: Store the secret in the organization-level GitHub secrets.
Store the secret in the repository-level GitHub secrets.
Encrypt the secret value and store the value in the repository. Store the decryption key in the repository-level GitHub secrets.
Encrypt the secret value and store the value in the repository. Store the decryption key in the organization-level GitHub secrets.

questions.explanation: GitHub Actions has a built-in 48-KB secret size limit. For secrets larger than 48 KB, the recommended approach is to encrypt the secret value yourself and store it in the repository, then store the decryption key in repository-level GitHub secrets. This way, the secret is encrypted at rest and only decryptable by the workflow using the key from the repo secrets, minimizing administrative overhead compared to organization-level management.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a project in Azure DevOps.  

You create the following YAML template named Template1.yml.  

steps:  

- script: npm install  
- script: yarn install  
- script: npm run compile  

You create the following pipeline named File1.yml.  

parameters:  

usersteps:  

- task: MyTask@1  
- script: echo Done  

You need to ensure that Template1.yaml runs before File1.yml.  

How should you update File1.yml?

options.text: parameters: usersteps: extends: template: template1.yml - task: MyTask@1 - script: echo Done
template: template1.yml parameters: usersteps: - task: MyTask@1 - script: echo Done
extends: template: templatel.yml parameters: usersteps: - task: MyTask@1 - script: echo Done
parameters: usersteps: - template: templatel.yml - task: MyTask@1 - script: echo Done

questions.explanation:
File1.yml must use the top-level `extends` keyword to force template1.yml to run as the pipeline's controlling template, with parameters passing the caller-specific `usersteps` list back into the template. Referencing template1.yml as an ordinary `template:` step (without `extends`) only inserts steps and cannot enforce that the template's steps execute before or wrap the calling pipeline's own steps.

**Learn more:** [Extend from a template](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/process/templates?view=azure-devops#extend-from-a-template)

You manage a project by using Azure Boards. You manage the project code by using GitHub.  
  
You have three work items that have IDs of 456, 457, and 458.  
  
You need to create a pull request that will be linked to all the work items. The solution must set the state of work item 456 to done.  
  
What should you add to the commit message?
questions.explanation: Azure Boards integration with GitHub uses the AB# prefix to reference work items. To link multiple work items (456, 457, 458) and set one to done, include both link references (#AB456, #AB457, #AB458) and the completion keyword (Completed #AB456). This syntax handles both requirements in a single commit message.

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
You manage a project by using Azure Boards. You manage the project code by using GitHub.  
  
You have three work items that have IDs of 456, 457, and 458.  
  
You need to create a pull request that will be linked to all the work items. The solution must set the state of work item 456 to done.  
  
What should you add to the commit message?
questions.explanation: When code lives in GitHub but work items live in Azure Boards, a commit or PR message links multiple work items using the AB# prefix, and applying a resolving keyword only to the first ID (e.g., "Fixes AB#456, AB#457, AB#458") closes just that item while still linking the others—matching the intent of this option despite its typographical inconsistencies. The remaining choices either omit the required AB prefix entirely or garble the syntax so badly that no valid link would be created.

To let Azure Resource Manager retrieve secrets from a key vault during template deployment, the vault's enabledForTemplateDeployment property must be set to true. This setting is exposed in the Azure portal as an 'Advanced access policy' checkbox ('Enable access to Azure Resource Manager for template deployment') and can be set via Set-AzKeyVaultAccessPolicy -EnabledForTemplateDeployment or az keyvault update --enabled-for-template-deployment true.

Once template deployment is enabled on the vault, access to the individual secrets is still governed separately. You use Git for source control.  
  
You need to commit a 3-GB ZIP file that contains virtual machines used for testing. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
• The file must be versioned.  

• The file must be associated with the corresponding code commits.  
  
Which two actions should you include in the solution? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Install the git-fat extension and associate the extension to ZIP files.
Install the Git LFS extension and associate the extension to ZIP files.
Install the git-stash extension and associate the extension to ZIP files.
Use GZip to compress the file before committing the file.
Store files in Azure Storage and enable blob versions.

questions.explanation: Installing Git LFS and associating it with the ZIP extension keeps only a small pointer file in the Git repository while the actual large binary is stored and versioned outside the repo, satisfying the requirement that the file stay tied to the corresponding code commits without bloating the repository. Pairing this with Azure Storage blob versioning gives the 3-GB file genuine, low-overhead version history, which plain Git (even with LFS alone) does not efficiently provide for very large binaries. **Learn more:** [Git Large File Storage](https://git-lfs.com/)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a hybrid cloud between Azure and Azure Stack.  

The company uses Azure DevOps for its full CI/CD pipelines. Some applications are built by using Erlang and Hack.  

You need to ensure that Erlang and Hack are supported as part of the build strategy across the hybrid cloud. The solution must minimize management overhead.  

What should you use to execute the build pipeline?

options.text: Azure DevOps self-hosted agents on Azure DevTest Labs virtual machines.
Azure DevOps self-hosted agents on Hyper-V virtual machines
Azure DevOps self-hosted agents on virtual machines that run on Azure Stack

questions.explanation: Custom languages like Erlang and Hack require a build environment configured with those language runtimes. A Microsoft-hosted agent (A) only supports standard languages, and DevTest Labs (B) or Hyper-V (C) don't address the hybrid cloud requirement. Azure Stack self-hosted agents (D) run in the on-premises/hybrid environment where Erlang and Hack tools are installed, enabling builds across the hybrid cloud infrastructure.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage projects by using Azure Boards.  
  
You have a current work item name itemA that is dependant on a work item named itemB.  
  
You need to define the dependency for itemA.  
  
What should you do in the web portal for Azure DevOps?

options.text: Add a Parent link to the user story of itemA.
From Backlogs, open the context menu, select Add link, and then select itemA. Set Link type to References and add the ID of itemB.
From itemA, open the Links tab, and then select Add link. Set Link type to References and add the ID of itemB.
From itemA, open the Links tab, and then select Add link. Set Link type to Successor and add the ID of itemB.

questions.explanation: Azure Boards models a dependency between two work items using the directional Predecessor-Successor link type pair, added from the item's Links tab via Add Link. "References" is not a recognized dependency link type in Azure Boards (it's used for shared test parameters), so of the given options only the Successor/Predecessor pairing actually establishes a tracked dependency relationship between itemA and itemB. **Learn more:** [Link type reference — Successor-Predecessor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/boards/queries/link-type-reference?view=azure-devops)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage an Azure DevOps project that contains package feeds.  
  
You need to make sure developers are able to unlist and deprecate packages, while adhering to the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which access level should you assign to the developers?
questions.explanation:
In Azure Artifacts, the Contributor role on a feed grants the ability to push, unlist, and deprecate packages, which is exactly the permission needed here. The Reader and Collaborator roles do not include rights to unlist or deprecate packages—Collaborator only adds the ability to save packages from upstream sources. The Owner role includes these capabilities too, but also grants full administrative control (deleting the feed, changing feed settings, managing permissions), which exceeds what is required and violates the principle of least privilege. Therefore, Contributor is the minimal role that satisfies the requirement.

**Learn more:** [Feed permissions - Azure Artifacts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/artifacts/feeds/feed-permissions)

You have an Azure web app that is deployed by using Azure Pipelines.  
  
You need to ensure that when a new version of the app is deployed to production, you can roll back to the previous version. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
• Minimize downtime during the deployment.  

• Minimize the time it takes for the rollback.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: a single web app and two deployment slots
a single web app and two deployment pipelines
two web apps and an Azure Standard Load Balancer
two web apps and an Azure Traffic Manager instance

questions.explanation: Azure App Service deployment slots enable you to deploy the new version to a staging slot and then perform a swap with production, minimizing downtime. If issues occur, you can quickly swap back to the previous version, achieving a rapid rollback. This approach requires only one web app with two slots, making it cost-effective while meeting both requirements.

You have an Azure web app that is deployed by using Azure Pipelines.  
  
You need to ensure that when a new version of the app is deployed to production, you can roll back to the previous version. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
• Minimize downtime during the deployment.  

• Minimize the time it takes for the rollback.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Feature isolation is the branching strategy in which one or more feature branches are created off the main branch (or off a development branch) specifically to develop a piece of new functionality in isolation from the rest of the team's work. This satisfies the stated technical requirement that new functionality be developed in isolation, since changes made in the feature branch don't affect other developers until the feature is complete and merged back, allowing conflicts and bugs to be managed independently of ongoing work in main or other branches. See Microsoft's Azure Repos guidance on feature isolation and branching strategies for further detail.

**Learn more:** [Manage feature isolation in TFVC - Azure Repos | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/tfvc/effective-feature-isolation-on-tfvc?view=azure-devops) · [Version Control - Branching strategies with TFVC - Azure Repos | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/tfvc/branching-strategies-with-tfvc?view=azure-devops)

You need to minimize the amount of disk space used by older packages in Azure Artifacts.  
  
What should you modify?

options.text: the retention settings of the project’s release
the retention settings of the project’s pipeline
the retention settings of the project’s tests
the retention settings of the company pipeline

questions.explanation: Azure Pipelines retention policies, configured at the project level, automatically remove old build artifacts and associated packages to free disk space. While package feeds have separate deletion capabilities, pipeline retention settings are the primary mechanism for minimizing disk usage of build-related npm packages in Azure Artifacts.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a private distribution group that includes both provisioned and unprovisioned devices.  
  
You need to distribute a new iOS application to this distribution group by using Microsoft Visual Studio App Center.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Request the Apple ID associated with the user of each device.
Register the devices on the Apple Developer portal.
Create an active subscription in App Center Test.
Add the device owner to the organization in App Center.

questions.explanation:
iOS ad-hoc app distribution requires that every target device's UDID be included in the app's provisioning profile. Devices that are not yet provisioned must first be registered on the Apple Developer portal so their UDIDs can be added to the provisioning profile; only then can App Center successfully install the app on those devices. This is a fundamental requirement of Apple's ad-hoc distribution model, independent of App Center itself.

**Learn more:** [Distribute iOS apps to devices - Visual Studio App Center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/appcenter/distribution/stores/apple-adhoc)
