You use a Git repository in Azure Repos to manage the source code of a web application. Developers currently commit changes directly to the default branch.  
  
You need to implement a change management procedure that meets the following requirements:  
  
- The default branch must be protected, and new changes must first be built in feature branches.  
- Changes must be reviewed and approved by at least one release manager before each merge.  
- Changes must be brought into the default branch by using pull requests.  
  
What should you configure in Azure Repos?

options.text: branch policies of the default branch
branch security of the default branch

questions.explanation:
Branch policies in Azure Repos let you protect a branch (such as main) by requiring that changes be submitted via pull request, enforcing a minimum number of reviewers who must approve the pull request, and preventing direct pushes to the protected branch. This directly satisfies all three requirements: protecting the default branch, mandating PR-based merges, and requiring reviewer (release manager) approval. Branch security controls user/group permissions on the branch but does not enforce PR workflows or approval gates, and the Services and Deployment pools settings in Project Settings relate to service connections and build/release agent pools, not branch protection or code review enforcement.

**Learn more:** [Improve code quality with branch policies - Azure Repos](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/git/branch-policies)

questions.domain: Implement an instrumentation strategy
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has built a web application. You need to recommend a solution that will automatically send a daily summary of the exceptions occurring in the application to Microsoft Teams.  
  
Which two Azure services should you recommend? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
*(Note: Each correct selection is worth one point.)*
questions.explanation:
Azure Application Insights automatically captures telemetry from the web application, including exception details, and stores it so it can be queried with Kusto Query Language (KQL). Azure Logic Apps provides workflow automation with a recurrence trigger to run on a schedule (daily), an action to run the Application Insights log query, and a built-in Microsoft Teams connector to post the resulting summary as a message to a Teams channel. Together these two services satisfy the requirement of automatically producing and delivering a daily exception summary to Teams, whereas Azure Pipelines, Azure DevOps Project, and Visual Studio App Center do not provide this combination of telemetry collection and scheduled cross-service messaging capability.

**Learn more:** [What is Application Insights? - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/app-insights-overview) · [Connectors for Azure Logic Apps - Microsoft Teams connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/teams/)

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
You use GitHub for source control and Azure Boards for project management. GitHub and Azure Boards are integrated.  
  
You plan to create a pull request in GitHub.  
  
You need to automatically link the request to an existing Azure Boards work item by using the text of AB#.  
  
To which two elements can you add the text? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation: When integrating GitHub pull requests with Azure Boards, the AB# syntax must appear in either the PR title or description to automatically link to a work item. Milestones, labels, and comments do not support work item linking through this mechanism.

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
You use GitHub for source control and Azure Boards for project management. GitHub and Azure Boards are integrated.  
  
You plan to create a pull request in GitHub.  
  
You need to automatically link the request to an existing Azure Boards work item by using the text of AB#.  
  
To which two elements can you add the text? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create an Azure Monitor Availability metric and alert.
Create an Azure Application Insights availability test and alert.
Write an Azure function and deploy the function to the specific regions.
Create an Azure Service Health alert for the specific regions.

questions.explanation:
Azure Application Insights availability tests (URL ping/standard tests) natively support running a ping test on a configurable interval, including every 5 minutes, and let you select specific Azure regions (test locations) from which the test is executed. An associated alert rule can then be configured to fire based on failures detected from those chosen locations, all through portal/ARM configuration without writing custom monitoring code, which satisfies the requirement to minimize development time. Deploying a custom Azure Function to multiple regions (option C) would require significant custom development. Azure Service Health (option D) reports on Azure platform incidents and planned maintenance, not application-level endpoint availability. There is no separate "Azure Monitor Availability metric" feature (option A) distinct from Application Insights availability tests that provides per-region ping testing and alerting.

**Learn more:** [Application Insights availability tests - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/availability) · [Monitor availability with URL ping tests - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/azure/azure-monitor/app/monitor-web-app-availability)

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
You use an Azure Pipelines pipeline to build and deploy an app.  
  
You have a custom test task that has the following inputs:  
  
• testResultsFiles: **/TEST-*.trx  

• searchFolder: $(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)  

• mergeTestResults: true  
  
Which format should you use for the input data of testResultsFiles?
questions.explanation: The .trx extension is produced by the Visual Studio Test Platform (VSTest), so the Publish Test Results task's testResultsFormat/testResultsFiles input must specify the VSTest format to correctly parse and publish `**/TEST-*.trx` files. NUnit, CTest, and JUnit expect XML formats with different schemas that do not match .trx output.

questions.domain: Design and implement processes and communications
questions.question:
You manage source code control and versioning by using GitHub.  
  
A large file is committed to a repository accidentally.  
  
You need to reduce the size of the repository. The solution must remove the file from the repository.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation: BFG Repo-Cleaner is a purpose-built tool for removing large files from Git repository history efficiently. It rewrites history to exclude specified files, reducing repository size. While Git LFS (B) manages large files going forward, it does not remove them from existing history.

questions.domain: Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.question:
Your company has an Azure DevOps environment that can only be accessed by Azure Active Directory users.  

You are instructed to make sure that the Azure DevOps environment can only be accessed from devices connected to the company's on-premises network.  

Which of the following actions should you take?

options.text: Assign the devices to a security group.
Configure Security in Project Settings from Azure DevOps.
Configure conditional access in Azure Active Directory.

questions.explanation: Azure AD Conditional Access policies enable you to define access requirements based on device location. By creating a conditional access policy that requires devices to be connected to the on-premises network, you can enforce location-based access control for Azure DevOps.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
You use GitHub to host container packages that use Semantic Versioning (SemVer).  
  
You have an app named App1. The current version of App1 is 11.2.0.  
  
You change the code of App1 to fix a bug that was introduced in version 10.5.1.  
  
Which version number should you assign to the release?
questions.explanation: Following semantic versioning, when the current production version is 11.2.0 and you're releasing a bug fix (regardless of which older version introduced the bug), you increment only the patch number (the third digit). Thus the version becomes 11.2.1. The original version in which the bug was introduced does not affect the versioning of the current release.

questions.domain: Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.question:
Your company is concerned that when developers introduce open source libraries, it creates licensing compliance issues.  

You need to add an automated process to the build pipeline to detect when common open source libraries are added to the code base.  

What should you use?
questions.explanation: Black Duck is a software composition analysis tool that detects open source components and checks them against company licensing policies. It can be integrated into Azure DevOps build pipelines to automatically scan for and alert on license compliance violations.

questions.domain: Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.question:
You use GitHub for source control.  

A file that contains sensitive data is committed accidentally to the Git repository of a project.  

You need to delete the file and its history form the repository.  

Which two tools can you use? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation: Both git filter-branch and BFG Repo-Cleaner can completely remove files and their history from a Git repository. BFG is often faster for large repositories, while git filter-branch provides more granular control. GitHub recommends either tool as a complete solution for removing sensitive data.

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
You have a GitHub repository that contains multiple versions of an Azure Pipelines template.  
  
You plan to deploy multiple pipelines that will use a template stored in the repository.  
  
You need to ensure that you use a fixed version of the template.  
  
What should you use to reference which version of the template repository to use?
questions.explanation:
Template documentation explicitly recommends pinning a repository resource to the 40-character Git SHA of a specific commit when a truly fixed version is required; a branch reference is not fixed because the branch tip keeps moving as new commits land on it.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use other repositories - pin to a ref](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/process/templates?view=azure-devops#use-other-repositories)

questions.domain: Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company develops an application named App1 that is deployed in production.  
  
As part of an update to App1, a new service is being added. This new service requires access to an application named App2, which is currently still in development.  
  
You need to ensure that you can deploy the App1 update before App2 becomes available, while also being able to enable the new service in App1 once App2 has been deployed.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a fork in the build.
Create a branch in the build.

questions.explanation:
A feature flag (feature toggle) lets you deploy code for a new capability while keeping it disabled in production. This decouples deployment from release: App1 can be updated and shipped immediately, and once the dependent App2 becomes available, the flag can simply be turned on to enable the new service—without requiring a new deployment. Forking, branching, and branch policies are source-control/build practices for managing code changes and enforcing quality gates during development; they do not provide a mechanism to control whether a feature is active in a running production application.

**Learn more:** [Feature flags in Azure DevOps / feature management overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-app-configuration/concept-feature-management)

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your application is made up of multiple Azure App Service web apps and Azure Functions.  
  
You need to evaluate the security posture of these web apps and functions.  
  
Which Azure feature would you use to obtain a recommendation regarding the security of the application?

options.text: Security & Compliance in Azure Log Analytics
Resource health in Azure Service Health
Smart Detection in Azure Application Insights
Compute & apps in Azure Security Center

questions.explanation:
Azure Security Center (now part of Microsoft Defender for Cloud) includes a 'Compute & apps' resource security hygiene section that specifically assesses App Service web apps and Azure Functions, providing prioritized security recommendations (such as enabling HTTPS-only, disabling remote debugging, using managed identities, and keeping TLS versions current) along with a secure score to help harden the application. This is the built-in Azure capability designed to evaluate and recommend security improvements for these compute resources, unlike Log Analytics' Security & Compliance solution, Service Health's Resource Health (which tracks availability, not security), or Application Insights Smart Detection (which flags performance/failure anomalies rather than security configuration issues).

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Microsoft Defender for Cloud (Azure Security Center)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-cloud-introduction) · [Protect your applications with Microsoft Defender for App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-app-service-introduction)

questions.domain: Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.question:
You have a project in Azure DevOps.  
  
You need to implement a new branching solution. The solution must ensure that all pull requests meet the following requirements:  
  
• Include linked work items.  

• Pass build validation policies.  

• Require at least three reviewers.  
  
What should you include in the solution?
questions.explanation: Branch policies in Azure DevOps are the mechanism for enforcing pull request requirements. They allow you to configure linked work item requirements, build validation policies, and reviewer count requirements. PR templates are documentation only, branch security controls access, and PR permissions control who can approve—none of these enforce the specific requirements mentioned.

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
You manage package feeds by using Azure Artifacts.  
  
You plan to create a new package feed that will include the following views:  
  
• @Local  

• @Latest  

• @Release  

• @Prerelease  
  
Which view should you create manually?
questions.explanation: Azure Artifacts feeds come with three default views: @Local, @Prerelease, and @Release. All other views must be created manually. @Latest is not created automatically, so it must be manually configured if needed. The other options (@Local, @Release, @Prerelease) are created by default.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Given a multi-tier application whose front end is hosted in Azure App Service, you need to determine the average load times of the application's pages. Which tool should you use?

options.text: the activity log of the App Service
the diagnostics logs of the App Service

questions.explanation:
Azure Application Insights is an Application Performance Management (APM) service that collects telemetry from web applications, including client-side browser telemetry such as page load times, AJAX call durations, and server response times. It provides built-in metrics and reports (e.g., the Browser/Page View Load Time metrics in the Performance and Browser blades) that let you monitor and analyze average page load times over time. The App Service activity log only records subscription-level control-plane operations (e.g., resource creation, configuration changes), the diagnostics logs capture platform/application logs but not detailed page load performance telemetry, and Azure Advisor only offers configuration and best-practice recommendations rather than real-time performance measurement.

**Learn more:** [Application Insights overview - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/app-insights-overview) · [Monitor web app performance - Application Insights JavaScript SDK](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/javascript)

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You use GitHub for source control of .NET applications.  

You need to deploy a documentation solution that meets the following requirements:  

✑ Documents will be written in Markdown as developers make code changes.  

✑ Changes to the documents will trigger the recompilation of a static website.  

✑ Users will access the documents from the static website.  

✑ Documents will be stored in a GitHub repository.  

Which two tools can you use to compile the website? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation: Jekyll is a widely-used static site generator for Markdown-based documentation, commonly used with GitHub Pages. DocFX is specifically designed for .NET projects and generates static API documentation from Markdown and C# source files. WordPress is dynamic; caret and Medium are not static site generators for local compilation.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are responsible for managing build and deployment pipelines in Azure DevOps.  
  
Your organization has a team of 500 developers, and new members are continually being added to this team.  
  
You need to automate the management of users and licenses wherever possible.  
  
Which of the following tasks must you still perform manually?
questions.explanation:
Azure DevOps can automate adding users, assigning entitlements, and updating group memberships by using Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) group rules, which automatically grant access levels and entitlements to users based on their group membership when they first sign in. However, procuring the licenses themselves — determining how many and which type of licenses to purchase and completing that purchase — is a commercial/administrative decision that Azure DevOps cannot automate; an administrator must manually acquire the licenses before they can be assigned through group rules.

**Learn more:** [Add group rule, assign access levels - Azure DevOps Services | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/organizations/accounts/assign-access-levels-by-group-membership?view=azure-devops) · [User and permissions management FAQs - Azure DevOps | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/organizations/accounts/faq-user-and-permissions-management?view=azure-devops)

questions.domain: Develop a security and compliance plan

options.text: Add a liveness probe to the YAML configuration of App1.
Add a readiness probe to the YAML configuration of App1.
Use Connection Monitor in Azure Network Watcher.
Use IP flow verify in Azure Network Watcher.

questions.explanation:
A liveness probe periodically checks whether the application running in a container instance is still functioning correctly. If the probe fails (for example, because the app stops responding), Azure Container Instances kills the container and restarts it, according to the group's restart policy. A readiness probe only determines whether the container is ready to receive traffic and does not cause a restart on failure. Network Watcher's Connection Monitor and IP flow verify are network diagnostic tools used to test connectivity and security rules, not to monitor application health or trigger container restarts. Configuring a livenessProbe section in the ACI YAML deployment is therefore the correct mechanism to restart ACI1 when App1 becomes unresponsive.

**Learn more:** [Set up liveness probe on container instance - Azure Container Instances | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-instances/container-instances-liveness-probe) · [Set up readiness probe on container instance - Azure Container Instances | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-instances/container-instances-readiness-probe)

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
You have Azure Pipelines and GitHub integrated as a source code repository.  

The build pipeline has continuous integration enabled.  

You plan to trigger an automated build whenever code changes are committed to the repository.  

You need to ensure that the system will wait until a build completes before queuing another build.  

What should you implement?
questions.explanation: Batch changes (batch: true) in Azure Pipelines causes the system to wait until the current build completes before queuing another build with accumulated changes, preventing concurrent builds. Path filters, scheduled builds, and branch filters don't control queuing behavior.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Consider the following Azure Policy definition:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783719550992-eth39d7i.png)  
  
You assign this policy to the Tenant Root Group.  
  
What effect does this policy have?

options.text: prevents all HTTP traffic to existing Azure Storage accounts
ensures that all traffic to new Azure Storage accounts is encrypted
prevents HTTPS traffic to new Azure Storage accounts when the accounts are accessed over the Internet
ensures that all data for new Azure Storage accounts is encrypted at rest

questions.explanation:
The policy's condition checks whether a resource is of type Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts and whether its supportsHttpsTrafficOnly property is not equal to true; when both conditions are met, the effect is deny. Because deny is evaluated during resource creation or update in Resource Manager mode, it blocks the creation (or modification) of any storage account that doesn't have supportsHttpsTrafficOnly set to true, effectively requiring all new storage accounts to enforce HTTPS-only (encrypted) traffic. It does not affect traffic to already-existing storage accounts (those are only flagged as non-compliant), and supportsHttpsTrafficOnly governs encryption of data in transit, not encryption at rest.

**Learn more:** [Azure Policy definitions deny effect - Azure Policy | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/effect-deny) · [Details of the policy definition structure policy rules - Azure Policy | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/definition-structure-policy-rule)

You use Git for source control.  
  
You enable GitHub code scanning.  
  
You raise a pull request from a non-default branch. In the code scanning output, you receive the following error message: “Analysis not found.”  
  
You need to ensure that the code scanning completes successfully for the pull request.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Add the name of the default branch to the on: push specification in the code scanning workflow.
Add the name of the non-default branch to the on:push specification in the code scanning workflow.
Delete the pull request, and then raise the request again from the default branch.
Update the code in the pull request.
Add a new workflow for code scanning.

questions.explanation: When GitHub code scanning reports 'Analysis not found' for a pull request from a non-default branch, two steps are required: (1) Add the non-default branch name to the on:push specification in the workflow so it runs on that branch, and (2) Update the code in the pull request to trigger a new analysis run. This ensures the branch is analyzed before comparison with the default branch.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
You use Azure Pipelines to build and deploy an app named App1.  
  
You plan to monitor App1 by using Application Insights.  
  
You create an Application Insights instance named AI1.  
  
You need to configure App1 to use AI1.  
  
Which file should you modify?
questions.explanation: The Application Insights instrumentation key or connection string that tells an app which AI resource to send telemetry to is a configuration value, not code, so it belongs in appsettings.json. The SDK wiring in Startup.cs only needs to be added once and does not change when you point the app at a different Application Insights instance.

questions.question:
You use Azure Pipelines to build and deploy an app named App1.  
  
You plan to monitor App1 by using Application Insights.  
  
You create an Application Insights instance named AI1.  
  
You need to configure App1 to use AI1.  
  
Which file should you modify?

options.text: From Microsoft Teams, run @azure pipelines subscribe https://dev.azure.com/Contoso/Project1.
From Azure Pipelines, add a Publish Build Artifacts task to Project1.
From Microsoft Teams, run @azure pipelines subscriptions.
From Azure Pipelines, enable continuous integration for Project1.

questions.explanation:
When you first subscribe to a project or pipeline with the `@azure pipelines subscribe` command, Teams creates a default subscription with no filters applied, so it reports on all build completion events regardless of outcome. To narrow notifications down to only failed builds, you must open subscription management by running `@azure pipelines subscriptions` in the channel. This lists the existing subscriptions for the channel, allowing you to select the subscription, apply the appropriate filter (Build status = Failed), and save the change (or remove the old unfiltered subscription and add a new filtered one). This is the documented workflow for customizing which events the Azure Pipelines Teams app reports, as described in Microsoft's Azure Pipelines Microsoft Teams integration documentation.

**Learn more:** [Azure DevOps integration with Microsoft Teams - Azure DevOps | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/integrations/microsoft-teams) · [Use Azure Repos with Microsoft Teams - Azure Repos | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/integrations/repos-teams?view=azure-devops)

questions.domain: Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.question:
You have an Azure DevOps project that contains a build pipeline. The build pipeline uses approximately 50 open source libraries.  

You need to ensure that all the open source libraries comply with your company's licensing standards.  

Which service should you use?
questions.explanation: Black Duck is purpose-built for open source license compliance, scanning dependencies and verifying they meet licensing standards. The community distinction is clear: use Black Duck for license compliance checks, and WhiteSource Bolt for broader open source vulnerability scanning in pipelines.

questions.domain: Implement an instrumentation strategy
questions.question:
You have an Azure DevOps project that contains a build pipeline. The build pipeline uses approximately 50 open source libraries.  

You need to ensure that all the open source libraries comply with your company's licensing standards.  

Which service should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Maven task in Azure Pipelines is designed to build Java projects and has built-in support for integrating with SonarQube analysis (via the 'Run SonarQube or SonarCloud Analysis' option and the Prepare Analysis Configuration task). This allows the pipeline to compile the Java code with Maven and simultaneously send code quality metrics to the existing SonarQube server. Grunt and Gulp are JavaScript/Node.js task runners unrelated to Java builds, and Octopus is a deployment tool, not a build or code-analysis task, so none of these are appropriate for analyzing Java code quality with SonarQube.

**Learn more:** [The Maven build task now simplifies SonarQube analysis - Azure DevOps Blog](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/devops/the-maven-build-task-now-simplifies-sonarqube-analysis/) · [Gradle or Maven project | SonarQube Community Build | Sonar Documentation](https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/devops-platform-integration/azure-devops-integration/adding-analysis-to-pipeline/gradle-or-maven-project)

questions.question:
You manage a project by using Azure Boards, and you manage the project code by using Azure Repos.  
  
You have a bug work item that has an ID of 123.  
  
You need to set the work item state to Resolved.  
  
What should you add to the commit message?
questions.explanation: Azure Boards recognizes resolution keywords (Fixes, Fixed, Fix, Resolves, Resolve, Resolved, Closes, Close, Closed) only when they precede the work item mention, e.g. \"Resolves #123\", and using a Resolve-family keyword transitions the linked bug to the Resolved state. The other choices place the ID before the keyword or use an unsupported keyword (\"Verifies\"), which Azure DevOps does not parse as a state-changing mention. **Learn more:** [Link work items to commits, pull requests, and changesets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/git/resolution-mentions)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to determine whether the underlined segment is correct.  
  
Your company has a multi-tier application that has its front end hosted in Azure App Service.  
  
To pinpoint the average load times of the application pages, you should make use of *Azure Event Hubs*.  
  
Select `No adjustment required` if the underlined segment is accurate. If the underlined segment is inaccurate, select the accurate option.
questions.explanation:
Azure Application Insights is an Application Performance Management (APM) feature of Azure Monitor designed to monitor live web applications. It automatically detects performance anomalies and includes analytics tools to help diagnose issues, including tracking of page view load times through its JavaScript SDK, which instruments client-side telemetry such as page load duration. Azure Event Hubs, by contrast, is a big data streaming platform and event ingestion service used to collect and process large volumes of data, and it does not provide application performance monitoring capabilities such as page load time tracking.

**Learn more:** [What is Application Insights? - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/app-insights-overview) · [Application Insights for web pages](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/javascript)

questions.question:
You configure Azure Application Insights and the shared service plan tier for a web app.  

You enable Smart Detection.  

You confirm that standard metrics are visible in the logs, but when you test a failure, you do not receive a Smart Detection notification.  

What prevents the Smart Detection notification from being sent?

options.text: You must enable the Snapshot Debugger for the web app.
Smart Detection uses the first 24 hours to establish the normal behavior of the web app.
The web app is configured to use the shared service plan tier.
You must restart the web app before Smart Detection is enabled.

questions.explanation: Smart Detection requires an initial 24-hour period to establish a baseline of normal application behavior before it can reliably detect and alert on anomalies. This delay is necessary to distinguish genuine failures from normal fluctuations.

questions.question:
You configure Azure Application Insights and the shared service plan tier for a web app.  

You enable Smart Detection.  

You confirm that standard metrics are visible in the logs, but when you test a failure, you do not receive a Smart Detection notification.  

What prevents the Smart Detection notification from being sent?

options.text: Create a service connection for GitHub.
From Import a Git repository, click Import.
Create a personal access token in Azure DevOps.

questions.explanation:
Azure DevOps Repos includes a native 'Import a Git repository' capability. On the Files page of the new (empty) Azure DevOps repository, selecting Import and supplying the GitHub repository's clone URL (with credentials if the source is private) copies all Git objects, branches, and history from GitHub into the Azure DevOps repo, effectively cloning it. This is documented as the standard method for importing/cloning an external Git repository, such as one from GitHub, into an Azure DevOps project.

**Learn more:** [Import a Git repository into a project - Azure Repos | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/git/import-git-repository?view=azure-devops)

questions.domain: Implement an instrumentation strategy
questions.question:
You are using GitHub as a source code repository.  

You create a client-side Git hook on the commit-msg event. The hook requires that each commit message contain a custom work item tag.  

You need to make a commit that does not have a work item tag.  

Which git commit parameter should you use?
questions.explanation: The --no-verify flag bypasses Git hooks, allowing commits even when pre-commit validation would normally fail. This parameter is documented in git-commit and git-hooks documentation as the standard way to skip hook verification.

questions.domain: Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.question:
You are using GitHub as a source code repository.  

You create a client-side Git hook on the commit-msg event. The hook requires that each commit message contain a custom work item tag.  

You need to make a commit that does not have a work item tag.  

Which git commit parameter should you use?
questions.explanation: To link a GitHub commit or pull request to Azure Boards work items and transition one of them, each work item ID must be prefixed with "AB#" and the list must be preceded by a state-transition keyword such as Fixes, Fixed, or Resolves. That keyword transitions only the first referenced work item (456) to its Completed/Resolved state category while still creating link references to the other two items. **Learn more:** [Link GitHub commits, pull requests, and issues to work items](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/boards/github/link-to-from-github)

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines

options.text: Install the Azure Boards app for Teams and configure a subscription to receive notifications in a channel.
Use Azure Automation to connect to the Azure DevOps REST API and notify the team members.
Use an Azure function to connect to the Azure DevOps REST API and notify the team members.
Install the Azure Pipelines app for Teams and configure a subscription to receive notifications in a channel.

questions.explanation: The Azure Pipelines app for Teams enables notifications for build and release events with minimal setup—just install and subscribe to events. Azure Boards handles work items; custom Automation or Functions solutions require additional development and API integration effort.

questions.domain: Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.question:
You have been tasked with strengthening the security of your team's development process.  

You need to suggest a security tool type for the Continuous Integration (CI) phase of the development process.  

Which of the following is the option you would suggest?
questions.explanation: Static code analysis scans source code without executing it during the CI phase, detecting security vulnerabilities before integration to the main codebase. Penetration testing and dynamic code analysis require live runtime environments. Threat modeling is a design-time activity, not a CI tool.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your development team is building a new web solution using the Microsoft Visual Studio IDE.  
  
You need to make a custom package available to all the developers. The package must be managed centrally, and the latest version must be automatically available for consumption in Visual Studio.  
  
Which three actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
(Note: Each correct selection is worth one point.)

options.text: Publish the package to a feed.
Create a new feed in Azure Artifacts.
Upload a package to a Git repository.
Add the package URL to the Environment settings in Visual Studio.
Add the package URL to the NuGet Package Manager settings in Visual Studio.
Create a Git repository in Azure Repos.

questions.explanation:
Azure Artifacts feeds provide a centralized location to store and manage packages (NuGet, npm, Maven, etc.) for a team or organization. To meet the requirement, you first create a feed in Azure Artifacts (the centralized package store), then publish the custom package to that feed so it is versioned and centrally managed, and finally configure the NuGet Package Manager settings in Visual Studio to reference that feed's URL as a package source — this lets Visual Studio automatically resolve and retrieve the latest version of the package for all developers. Git repositories are not package feeds and don't provide package versioning/consumption features, and Visual Studio has no 'Environment settings' area for specifying package URLs.

**Learn more:** [Get started with NuGet packages in Azure Artifacts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/artifacts/get-started-nuget) · [Create and share Azure Artifacts feeds](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/artifacts/feeds/feeds-overview)

You use Azure Artifacts to host NuGet packages that you create.  
  
You need to make one of the packages available to anonymous users outside your organization. The solution must minimize the number of publication points.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Change the feed URL of the package
Create a new feed for the package
Promote the package to a release view.
Publish the package to a public NuGet repository.

questions.explanation:
Azure Artifacts feeds live within an Azure DevOps organization and require authenticated access; they cannot be opened up for anonymous, unauthenticated consumption by users outside the organization. The only way to make a package available to anonymous external users is to publish it to a public NuGet repository (such as nuget.org), which is designed for anonymous, public consumption. This requires only one additional publish action, minimizing publication points, whereas changing the feed URL or creating a new feed keeps the package within the authenticated Azure DevOps boundary, and promoting to a release view only affects the package's view state within the existing feed rather than its external visibility.

**Learn more:** [Publish NuGet packages with Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/artifacts/nuget?view=azure-devops) · [Publish and download universal packages - Azure Artifacts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/artifacts/quickstarts/universal-packages)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a project in Azure DevOps named Project1. Project1 contains a pipeline that builds a container image named Image1 and pushes Image1 to an Azure container registry named ACR1. Image1 uses a base image that is stored in Docker Hub.  
  
You need to ensure that Image1 is updated automatically whenever the base image is updated.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Enable the Azure Event Grid resource provider and subscribe to registry events.
Add a Docker Hub service connection to Azure Pipelines.
Create and run an Azure Container Registry task.
Create a service hook in Project1.

questions.explanation:
Azure Container Registry Tasks provide a base image update trigger capability: ACR Tasks can track the dependencies of an image (including base images referenced from external registries such as Docker Hub) and automatically rebuild and push the derived image whenever the base image changes. Creating and running an ACR Task configured with this trigger fulfills the requirement to keep Image1 automatically updated when its Docker Hub base image changes, without needing manual pipeline runs, Event Grid subscriptions, service connections, or service hooks.

**Learn more:** [Automate image builds when a base image is updated - Azure Container Registry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-tutorial-base-image-update)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure pipeline that is used to deploy an app named App1.  
  
You need to ensure that new versions of App1 are released only if they exceed performance baselines. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation: A deployment gate is the mechanism in Azure Pipelines that automatically evaluates external criteria—such as an Azure Monitor query against performance metrics—before allowing a release to proceed, with no custom scripting or manual review needed. An Azure Monitor alert on its own only notifies of a problem; it does not block or gate a release, so it cannot by itself stop a substandard build from being promoted. **Learn more:** [Release gates and approvals overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/release/approvals/gates)

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are monitoring the health and performance of an Azure web app using Azure Application Insights.  
  
You need to ensure that an alert is sent when the web app experiences a sudden increase in performance issues and failures.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Smart Detection in Application Insights automatically analyzes the telemetry your app sends and detects anomalies such as a sudden rise in failure rates or unusual performance degradation compared to normal patterns. When it detects such an issue, it proactively sends near real-time alerts (via email or the Azure portal) without requiring you to manually configure alert thresholds. This differs from custom events (used to log custom telemetry manually), Application Insights Profiler (used to trace and identify slow code paths in requests), usage analysis (used to analyze user behavior and engagement), and continuous export (used to export raw telemetry data to external storage).

**Learn more:** [Application Insights Smart Detection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/proactive-diagnostics)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],After adding the virtual machines as managed nodes in Azure Automation State Configuration, you need to configure the managed computers in Pool7.  
  
What should you do next?

options.text: Modify the RefreshMode property of the Local Configuration Manager (LCM).
Run the Register-AzureRmAutomationDscNode Azure Powershell cmdlet.
Modify the ConfigurationMode property of the Local Configuration Manager (LCM).

questions.explanation:
The Local Configuration Manager (LCM) runs on every DSC target node and its ConfigurationMode property determines how the node applies and maintains its desired state configuration. The available values are ApplyOnly (apply once, no ongoing drift correction), ApplyAndMonitor (apply and log drift only, the default), and ApplyAndAutoCorrect (apply, detect drift, and automatically reapply the configuration to correct it). Since the VMs in Pool7 have already been registered as managed nodes, the remaining step needed to ensure the servers continue to comply with their assigned configuration—correcting any drift that occurs after initial deployment—is to modify the ConfigurationMode property of the LCM (typically setting it to ApplyAndAutoCorrect). This setting change currently requires re-registering the node, as DSC LCM values set during initial registration can only be altered through re-registration.

**Learn more:** [Enable Azure Automation State Configuration - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/automation/automation-dsc-onboarding) · [Register-AzureRmAutomationDscNode (AzureRM.Automation) - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/azurerm.automation/register-azurermautomationdscnode?view=azurermps-6.13.0)

You have an Azure subscription that contains a Log Analytics workspace named WS1 and a virtual machine named VM1.  
  
You need to install the Microsoft Enterprise Cloud Monitoring extension on VM1.  
  
Which two values are required to configure the extension? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.

options.text: the system-assigned managed identity of VM1

questions.explanation: The Microsoft Enterprise Cloud Monitoring (OMS) extension for Azure VMs requires the workspace ID and primary/secret key to authenticate and connect to the Log Analytics workspace. The workspace ID identifies which workspace receives monitoring data, and the secret key authenticates the connection. Other identifiers such as subscription ID or resource ID are not required for extension configuration.

You use Azure DevOps processes to build and deploy code.  
  
You need to compare how much time is spent troubleshooting issues found during development and how much time is spent troubleshooting issues found in released code.  
  
Which KPI should you use?
questions.explanation: The defect escape rate measures the proportion of defects discovered in production relative to those found during development and testing. This KPI directly compares troubleshooting effort in released code versus development, and is a standard metric for assessing development process quality.

questions.question:
You plan to publish build artifacts by using an Azure pipeline.  
  
You need to create an .artifactignore file that meets the following requirements:  
  
• Includes all files in the build output folder and all subfolders  

• Excludes files that have the .dll extension  
  
What should you include in the file?
questions.explanation: The pattern **/*!*.dll in .artifactignore matches all files in all directories except those ending with .dll. The ** glob pattern captures all directories recursively, while the negation pattern (!*.dll) excludes files with the .dll extension, achieving the requirements of including all files but excluding DLLs.

questions.question:
You have a GitHub repository.  
  
You need to ensure that all the code in the repository is scanned for vulnerabilities.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation: CodeQL is a semantic code analysis engine that performs static analysis to detect security vulnerabilities, coding errors, and logic flaws in your own codebase. Dependabot (A) focuses on dependencies, branch protection rules (B) enforce reviews, and the Advisory Database (D) is a reference tool—only CodeQL scans the repository's source code for vulnerabilities.

questions.question:
You have an Azure virtual machine that is monitored by using Azure Monitor.  

The virtual machine has the Azure Log Analytics agent installed.  

You plan to deploy the Service Map solution from the Azure Marketplace.  

What should you deploy to the virtual machine to support the Service Map solution?
questions.explanation: The Dependency agent is required for Service Map to function alongside the Log Analytics agent. It maps process dependencies and network connections between systems. Telegraf is for metrics collection; WAD is for diagnostics; Azure Monitor Agent (still emerging) hasn't fully replaced the Dependency agent for Service Map.

questions.domain: Implement an instrumentation strategy
questions.question:
Your company is building a new solution in Java.  

The company currently uses a SonarQube server to analyze the code of .NET solutions.  

You need to analyze and monitor the code quality of the Java solution.  

Which task types should you add to the build pipeline?
questions.explanation: Maven is the Java build tool with integrated SonarQube analysis support. It provides task types for compiling, testing, and analyzing Java code with SonarQube. CocoaPods (iOS), Xcode (macOS), and Gulp (JavaScript) are for different platforms and languages.

questions.domain: Implement an instrumentation strategy
questions.question:
Your company is building a new solution in Java.  

The company currently uses a SonarQube server to analyze the code of .NET solutions.  

You need to analyze and monitor the code quality of the Java solution.  

Which task types should you add to the build pipeline?

options.text: Modify the load balancer settings of VMSS1.
Upload a custom script file to sa1.
Modify the Custom Script extension settings of VMSS1.
Update the configuration of a virtual machine in VMSS1.

questions.explanation: Limited canary-style testing for a VM Scale Set whose app is managed by the Custom Script Extension is done by staging the new version's script in the storage account (C), repointing the extension configuration to the new script (D), and manually upgrading only a single instance (or a few) rather than the whole set (E) — the documented Microsoft pattern for canary deployments on VMSS. Changing the load balancer (A) doesn't control which instances run the new code, and redeploying the whole scale set (B) would push the change to every VM instead of a limited subset.

questions.domain: Develop a security and compliance plan

options.text: Add a Run Inline Azure PowerShell task to the pipeline.
Add a PowerShell task to the pipeline and run Set-AzureKeyVaultSecret.
Add an Azure Key Vault task to the pipeline.
Add Azure Key Vault references to Azure Resource Manger templates.

questions.explanation: The Azure Key Vault task in Azure DevOps pipelines retrieves secrets from Key Vault at runtime and injects them as secure pipeline variables, preventing credential exposure in pipeline configuration or logs. This is the direct pipeline-level solution for preventing infrastructure credential leaks. ARM template references (option D) are for infrastructure deployment, not pipeline security, and the PowerShell-based options expose more risk.

You have an Azure DevOps organization named Contoso that includes a project named Project1.  
  
You provision an Azure key vault named Keyvault1.  
  
You need to reference secrets from Keyvault1 in a build pipeline belonging to Project1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Add a secure file to Project1.
Create a variable group in Project1.
Configure the security policy of Contoso.

questions.explanation:
To use Azure Key Vault secrets in an Azure Pipelines build, you must first create a variable group in the project's Pipeline Library, then configure it to link secrets from an Azure key vault by specifying the Azure subscription (service connection) and selecting Keyvault1, followed by choosing which secrets to expose as pipeline variables. This variable group is then referenced in the pipeline definition to make the secrets available during the build. Creating a secure file is unrelated to Key Vault integration, XAML build services are a deprecated feature not used for this scenario, and modifying the organization's security policy is not a prerequisite for linking a key vault to a variable group.

**Learn more:** [Add and use variable groups - Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/library/variable-groups?view=azure-devops) · [Link secrets from an Azure key vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/release/azure-key-vault)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A project in Azure DevOps is used to build a new web application. The company relies on ServiceNow for change management. You need to make sure a change request is processed before any components can be deployed to the production environment.  
  
Which two approaches can be used to integrate ServiceNow into the Azure DevOps release pipeline? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
(Choose two. Each correct selection is worth one point.)

options.text: Define a deployment control that invokes the ServiceNow REST API.
Define a pre-deployment gate before the deployment to the Prod stage.
Define a deployment control that invokes the ServiceNow SOAP API.
Define a post-deployment gate after the deployment to the QA stage.

questions.explanation:
The official ServiceNow Change Management extension for Azure Pipelines provides two integration mechanisms: a pre-deployment gate that blocks progression to a stage (such as Prod) until the linked ServiceNow change request satisfies the configured condition, and an agentless deployment task/control that calls the ServiceNow REST API to create, query, or update a change request during the release. Using either mechanism on the Prod stage's pre-deployment conditions ensures deployment cannot proceed until the change request has been processed. The integration communicates with ServiceNow over its REST API (not SOAP), and the control must be applied before the Prod deployment, not after a QA deployment, to actually gate the production release.

**Learn more:** [Integrate with ServiceNow change management - Azure Pipelines | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/release/approvals/servicenow?view=azure-devops) · [ServiceNow Change Management Extension - Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscs-rm.vss-services-servicenowchangerequestmanagement)

You are building an open-source solution hosted in a GitHub repository. You create a new public project in Azure DevOps and plan to use Azure Pipelines for continuous integration builds. The solution must use the GitHub Checks API.  
  
Which authentication type should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Pipelines supports three ways to authorize access to a GitHub repository: a GitHub App, OAuth, or a personal access token (PAT). Only the GitHub App authorization type supports the GitHub Checks API, which surfaces detailed build/check results, annotations, and status directly within GitHub pull requests. Because the requirement specifies use of the Checks API, the GitHub App integration must be used.\
\
**Learn more:** [Connect to GitHub - Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/repos/github?view=azure-devops)

questions.explanation: Line 4 should be modified from the SDK image (mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:7.0) to the runtime image (mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:7.0). options.text: Create a Microsoft Intune device compliance policy.
Deploy a certificate from an internal certification authority (CA) to each device.
Register the application in the iTunes store.
Onboard the devices into Microsoft Intune.
Distribute a new release of the application.
Register the IDs of the devices in the Apple Developer portal.

questions.explanation: To manually test an iOS app on a limited set of physical devices without a public release, Apple's ad-hoc distribution model must be used. This requires registering the UDIDs of the specific test devices in the Apple Developer portal so they can be included in the ad-hoc provisioning profile, and then distributing a new build/release of the app (for example through App Center Distribute connected to an Azure DevOps release pipeline) to those registered testers. Registering the app in the iTunes store would make it publicly available, which contradicts the requirement, and Intune enrollment/compliance policies and CA certificate deployment address device management, not ad-hoc app testing distribution for iOS.

You have an on-premises app named App1 that accesses Azure resources by using credentials stored in a configuration file.  

You plan to upgrade App1 to use an Azure service principal.  

What is required for App1 to programmatically sign in to Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)?

options.text: the application ID, a client secret, and the object ID
a client secret, the object ID, and the tenant ID
the application ID, a client secret, and the tenant ID
the application ID, a client secret, and the subscription ID

questions.explanation: Service principal authentication requires three components: the application ID (client ID identifying the service principal), a client secret (the credential), and the tenant ID (Azure AD tenant identifier). Object ID is internal to Azure AD; subscription ID is for resource management, not authentication.

You plan to upgrade App1 to use an Azure service principal.  

What is required for App1 to programmatically sign in to Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)?
questions.explanation: Azure App Configuration is purpose-built for managing configuration data across applications. It supports feature flags, hierarchical key-value pairs, change tracking (auditing changes over 30 days), role-based access control (RBAC), and centralized sharing of configuration values across multiple applications. Azure Key Vault focuses on secrets, Cosmos DB is for data storage, and App Service is a compute platform.

options.text: Create a branch protection rule for the feature branches.
Create a branch protection rule for the main branch.

questions.explanation:
A CODEOWNERS file lets you designate the security department as required reviewers for the relevant paths, and a branch protection rule on the main branch that requires their approval (plus status checks) blocks any pull request from merging until that review happens. Signed commits only verify authorship/integrity and don't enforce a review gate, and protecting feature branches has no effect on what is allowed to merge into main.

**Learn more:** [About code owners](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners)

You use an Azure Pipelines pipeline to build and test an app named App1.  
  
Your company’s development department works in the feature branches.  
  
You need to ensure that a pull request will merge into the main branch only when testing covers more than 90 percent of the code.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure a branch policy for the feature branches.
Configure a branch policy for the main branch.
Create a Publish Test Results task,
Create a code coverage configuration YAML file.

questions.explanation: Branch policies are configured on the target branch (main) to enforce requirements before merges. To require >90% code coverage before PRs can merge into main, you configure the policy on the main branch itself. Feature branch policies would prevent merges into features (not needed). Tasks and configuration files set up coverage collection, not merge policies.

questions.explanation: BFG Repo-Cleaner and git filter-repo are both valid tools for removing sensitive files from git history. BFG (option C) is often preferred for simpler cases like deleting a single file and requires force push to rewrite history. Option E (git filter-repo) is more powerful for complex history rewrites. Either would work, but BFG is the simpler solution for this straightforward file removal.

questions.question:
You have a public GitHub repository named Public1.  
  
A commit is made to Public1. The commit contains a pattern that matches a regular expression.  
  
Who is notified first when the commit is made?

options.text: the administrator of the GitHub organization

questions.explanation: GitHub's secret scanning service detects patterns that match known secret formats and notifies the associated service provider (secret scanning partner) first, directly on the provider's side. This happens before any notification reaches the repository owner, committer, or administrator. The partner can then take immediate action to revoke compromised credentials.

You have a public GitHub repository named Public1.  
  
A commit is made to Public1. The commit contains a pattern that matches a regular expression.  
  
Who is notified first when the commit is made?
questions.explanation:
The Cherry-pick pull request action in Azure DevOps allows you to take a specific commit (or a subset of commits) from a pull request and apply it to a new branch, rather than including all the changes from the entire pull request. This lets you create a branch containing only a portion of the PR's code, which can then be merged into the target branch later. Other actions like Revert apply to the whole PR's changes, Reactivate reopens an abandoned PR, and Approve with suggestions is merely a review vote option — none of these create a branch with a partial set of the PR's changes.

**Learn more:** [Cherry-pick or revert changes with pull requests - Azure Repos](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/git/cherry-pick?view=azure-devops)

Splunk is third-party; Azure Advisor focuses on optimization recommendations; App Service logs provide basic diagnostics, not performance metrics.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 50 Node.js-based projects that you scan by using WhiteSource. Each project includes Package.json, Package-lock.json, and Npm-shrinkwrap.json files.  

You need to minimize the number of libraries reports by WhiteSource to only the libraries that you explicitly reference.  

What should you do?

options.text: Configure the File System Agent plug-in.
Add a devDependencies section to Package-lock.json.

questions.explanation: To minimize WhiteSource reporting to only explicitly referenced libraries, configure WhiteSource to exclude development dependencies. The intended answer references excluding devDependencies (which are only needed for development, not production); however, there is a noted discrepancy in the question where it references package-lock.json instead of package.json. The solution principle is correct: filter out transitive and development-only dependencies to report only directly referenced production libraries.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a build pipeline configured in Azure Pipelines. You create a Slack App Integration. You need to send build notifications to a Slack channel named #Development. What should you do first?
questions.explanation:
Sending Azure Pipelines build notifications to a Slack channel via a custom Slack app (incoming webhook) requires creating a service hook subscription in the Azure DevOps project. On the project's Service Hooks page, you create a subscription, select the build-related trigger event, and supply the Slack webhook URL obtained from the Slack app integration so that build notifications are posted to the specified channel. Service connections are unrelated to notification delivery (they authorize pipelines to access external resources such as Azure subscriptions or container registries), and project-level or global notifications route through Azure DevOps' built-in email/Teams notification system rather than Slack webhooks.

**Learn more:** [Create a service hook with Slack - Azure DevOps | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/service-hooks/services/slack?view=azure-devops) · [Integrate with Slack - Azure Pipelines | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/integrations/slack?view=azure-devops)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage projects by using Azure Boards.  
  
You have a current work item name itemA that is dependant on a work item named itemB.  
  
You need to define the dependency for itemA.  
  
What should you do in the web portal for Azure DevOps?

options.text: From itemA, open the Links tab, and then select Add link. Set Link type to Related and add the ID of itemB.
From Backlogs, open the context menu, select Add link, and then select itemA. Set Link type to Successor and add the ID of itemB.
From itemA, open the Links tab, and then select Add link. Set Link type to References and add the ID of itemB.
From Queries, open the context menu, select Add link, and then select Existing Item. Set Link type to Affected By and add the ID of itemB.

questions.explanation: In Azure DevOps, dependencies are defined using predecessor/successor link types. Since itemA depends on itemB, itemB is the predecessor and itemA is the successor. From Backlogs, select itemA, add a link, set the link type to 'Successor', and reference itemB's ID to establish that itemA succeeds (depends on) itemB.

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.explanation:
Azure Artifacts feeds allow multiple package versions to exist under one feed, and each feed automatically includes three views: @Local, @Prerelease, and @Release. By promoting packages through these views as they pass testing and validation, you can restrict consumers to only the @Release view, ensuring that in-development or unvalidated builds (which remain in @Local) are not exposed. This lets a single feed host multiple builds of a package while controlling which ones are released to consumers.

**Learn more:** [What are feed views? - Azure Artifacts | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/artifacts/concepts/views?view=azure-devops) · [Promote packages and manage feed views - Azure Artifacts | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/artifacts/feeds/views?view=azure-devops)

During a code review, you find numerous quality issues, including many modules that contain unused variables and empty catch blocks. You need to recommend a solution to improve the quality of the code. What should you recommend?

options.text: In a Grunt build task, select Enabled from Control Options.
In a Maven build task, select Run PMD.
In a Xcode build task, select Use xcpretty from Advanced.
In a Gradle build task, select Run Checkstyle.

questions.explanation:
PMD is a static code analyzer designed to detect common programming flaws in Java code, including unused variables, unused parameters, unnecessary object creation, and empty catch blocks. The Azure DevOps Maven build task includes a built-in 'Run PMD' (Run PMD Analysis) option that runs this analysis as part of the build and generates a report listing all violations found, including the number of unused variables and empty catch blocks. Checkstyle, used in the Gradle task, focuses on enforcing coding style and formatting conventions rather than detecting these specific logic-level defects, making it less suited to this scenario. The Grunt and Xcode options listed are unrelated to Java static analysis.

**Learn more:** [The Maven build task now supports PMD analysis out of the box - Azure DevOps Blog](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/devops/the-maven-build-task-now-supports-pmd-analysis-out-of-the-box/) · [Maven@3 - Maven v3 task | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/reference/maven-v3?view=azure-pipelines)

questions.question:
You manage code by using GitHub.  
  
You need to ensure that repository owners are notified if a new vulnerable dependency or malware is found in their repository.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure branch protection rules for each repository.
Subscribe all the repository owners to the GitHub Advisory Database.

questions.explanation: Dependabot is GitHub's automated dependency scanning tool that detects vulnerable dependencies and malware in repositories and alerts repository owners. It also offers automatic pull requests to remediate vulnerabilities. CodeQL scanning is for code security analysis, branch protection rules are for merge controls, and the GitHub Advisory Database is a reference resource, not a notification mechanism.

Your Azure subscription includes an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
You are setting up a build pipeline in Azure Pipelines that will contain a task named Task1. Task1 will authenticate using an Azure AD service principal.  
  
Which three values should you configure for Task1? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Authenticating with an Azure AD service principal requires the principal's identifying and authenticating credentials: the tenant (directory) ID that specifies which Azure AD tenant the service principal is registered in, the application (client) ID — the App ID — that uniquely identifies the service principal/app registration, and the client secret that serves as the password-equivalent credential proving the service principal's identity. The subscription ID is used to scope the target Azure resources but is not part of the service principal's authentication credentials, and the object ID is not used in this authentication configuration.

**Learn more:** [Use Service Principals and Managed Identities - Azure DevOps | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/integrate/get-started/authentication/service-principal-managed-identity?view=azure-devops) · [Use an Azure Resource Manager service connection - Azure Pipelines | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/library/connect-to-azure?view=azure-devops)

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
You have an Azure DevOps organization named Contoso.  

You need to recommend an authentication mechanism that meets the following requirements:  

✑ Supports authentication from Git  

✑ Minimizes the need to provide credentials during authentication  

What should you recommend?

options.text: personal access tokens (PATs) in Azure DevOps
user accounts in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)
managed identities in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)

questions.explanation: A personal access token lets a user authenticate Git operations against Azure Repos without repeatedly supplying their organizational username and password — once cached by Git or a credential manager, the PAT is reused automatically until it expires. This satisfies both requirements (Git-compatible authentication and minimized credential prompting) better than alternate credentials, which reuse the account password directly on every prompt.

questions.question:
You have an Azure DevOps organization named Contoso.  

You need to recommend an authentication mechanism that meets the following requirements:  

✑ Supports authentication from Git  

✑ Minimizes the need to provide credentials during authentication  

What should you recommend?

options.text: Add a status check to the policies of the branch used by your company's development department.
Add a status check to the policies of the main branch.
Add a service hook to the project.
Limit the job authorization scope to the current project for all the release pipelines.

questions.explanation:
Since App1 is deployed from code that lands on the main branch, requiring the custom security tool as a status check in the main branch's policies guarantees no pull request can complete, and therefore no code can reach the deployment stage, until the tool reports success. Gating only the branch used by the development department would leave other paths into main (such as hotfixes or merges from other teams) unchecked, so deployed code would not be reliably validated.

**Learn more:** [Branch policies and settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/git/branch-policies)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a project in Azure DevOps named Project1. Project1 contains a build pipeline named Pipe1 that builds an application named App1.  
  
You have an agent pool named Pool1 that contains a Windows Server 2019-based self-hosted agent. Pipe1 uses Pool1.  
  
You are planning to implement another project named Project2. Project2 will have a build pipeline named Pipe2 that builds an application named App2.  
  
App1 and App2 have conflicting dependencies.  
  
You need to minimize the possibility that the two build pipelines will conflict with each other. The solution must also minimize infrastructure costs.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add a Docker Compose task to the build pipelines.
Change the self-hosted agent to use Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 8.

questions.explanation:
Azure Pipelines allows a job to run inside a Docker container on a self-hosted agent by defining a container job. This isolates each pipeline's build tools and dependencies within their own container, so App1's and App2's conflicting dependencies never interact, even though both pipelines still use the same underlying self-hosted agent in Pool1. This avoids the cost of provisioning and maintaining additional agent infrastructure (unlike adding another self-hosted agent), and directly resolves the dependency isolation problem, which a Docker Compose task (intended for multi-container image build/push orchestration) or an OS change to the agent would not address.

**Learn more:** [Container jobs - Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/process/container-phases)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains an Azure Pipelines pipeline named Pipeline1 and a user named User1. Pipeline1 is used to build and test an app named App1. User1 is assigned the Contributors role for Pipeline1.  
  
You plan to test App1 by using an Azure Deployment Environments environment.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can provision the environment. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation: The Deployment Environments User role is the minimal role required to provision environments in Azure Deployment Environments. When assigned at the project level, this role allows users to view environment types, create environments, and manage their own deployments while adhering to the principle of least privilege. DevCenter Project Admin would be excessive, Contributors is too broad, and Build Administrators is unrelated to environment provisioning.

You have a project in Azure DevOps named App Project that is used to develop an app named App1. App1Project has an Azure Boards team dashboard that is used to monitor the progress of App1 and track work items.  
  
You need to track how long it takes to close a work item once work for the item has commenced.  
  
Which type of widget should you add to the dashboard?
questions.explanation: Cycle time measures the duration from when work has commenced (started) to when it is completed or closed. This directly addresses the requirement to track how long items take once work begins. Lead time measures from request to completion, sprint burndown tracks work within a sprint period, and velocity measures work completed per sprint—none capture the commenced-to-closed interval.

Git is a distributed version control system, meaning every developer's local repository contains a full copy of the project's history. This enables developers to commit changes, create branches, and browse the entire history offline, then synchronize with the shared remote repository once connectivity is restored. In contrast, Team Foundation Version Control (TFVC) is a centralized system that generally requires a connection to the server for history and most source control operations, making it unsuitable for frequent offline work with full history access.

**Learn more:** [Azure Repos - Choose the right version control for your project](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/tfvc/comparison-git-tfvc)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company hosts a web application in Azure and uses Azure Pipelines for build and release management of the application.  
  
Stakeholders report that the past few releases have negatively affected system performance.  
  
You configure alerts in Azure Monitor.  
  
You need to ensure that new releases are only deployed to production if they meet defined performance baseline criteria in the staging environment first.  
  
What should you use to prevent the deployment of releases that fail to meet the performance baseline?
questions.explanation:
Azure Pipelines release gates let you specify conditions that must be satisfied before a release is promoted to the next stage (such as production). Gates can automatically query external services—including Azure Monitor alerts—as part of pre-deployment conditions, and the release is blocked from proceeding if the criteria aren't met. This directly supports validating performance baselines in staging before allowing deployment to production. Triggers only control when a pipeline stage starts, not whether it passes a quality bar, and Azure Scheduler jobs/Azure Functions are not themselves the gating mechanism in Azure Pipelines.

**Learn more:** [Release deployment control using approvals and gates - Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/release/approvals/gates)

questions.question:
You have a GitHub repository that contains workflows. The workflows contain steps that execute predefined actions. Each action has one or more versions.  

You need to request the specific version of an action to execute.  

Which three attributes can you use to identify the version? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation: GitHub Actions can be versioned using: (A) commit SHA hashes (most reliable for immutable reference), (B) Git tags (human-friendly semantic version labels), and (D) branch names (references latest commit on that branch). Runner specifies the execution environment; serial is not an applicable versioning mechanism.
