lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a private GitHub repository.  
  
You need to display the commit status of the repository on Azure Boards.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Configure multi-factor authentication (MFA) for your GitHub account.
Add the Azure Pipelines app to the GitHub repository.
Add the Azure Boards app to the repository.
Create a GitHub action in GitHub.

questions.explanation:
The Azure Pipelines app, available on GitHub Marketplace, is the component that integrates Azure Pipelines with a GitHub repository. Installing (adding) this app to the repository authorizes Azure DevOps to access the repo and enables Azure Pipelines to post build and commit status information back to GitHub (as GitHub Checks/commit statuses), which is what allows that status to be tracked and displayed through Azure Boards' traceability features (such as the Development/Deployment controls on work items). For a private repository, this app must be explicitly added/authorized before any commit status can be reported, making it the required first step. The Azure Boards app (option C) instead handles linking GitHub commits, pull requests, and issues to work items — it does not report commit/build status. MFA configuration and GitHub Actions are unrelated to this integration.

**Learn more:** [Build GitHub repositories - Azure Pipelines | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/repos/github?view=azure-devops) · [Configure pipelines to support integration - Azure DevOps | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/integrations/configure-pipelines-work-tracking?view=azure-devops)

questions.question:
You manage a project by using Azure Board, and you manage the project code by using Azure Repos.  
  
You have a bug work item that has an ID of 123.  
  
You need to set the work item state to Resolved.  
  
What should you add to the commit message?
questions.explanation: In Azure Repos, the keywords 'Fix', 'Fixes', or 'Fixed' followed by work item ID automatically link commits to work items and transition them to resolved state. The format is 'Fixes #123' for work item 123. Option B uses incorrect format (AB-123 prefix) and 'Resolves' keyword, which is not recognized by Azure Repos for this purpose.

To compile an Internet Information Services (IIS) web application that runs docker, you should use a Default build agent pool.  

Select `No adjustment required` if the underlined segment is accurate. If the underlined segment is inaccurate, select the accurate option.
questions.explanation: To compile an Internet Information Services (IIS) web application that runs in Docker containers, you must use a Hosted Windows Container agent pool, not a Default pool. The Hosted Windows Container pool provides both Windows and Docker support needed for this scenario.

questions.question:
You have a GitHub repository that contains multiple workflows and a secret stored at the environment level.  
  
You need to ensure that the secret can be used by all the workflows.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Recreate the secret at the organization level.
Recreate the secret at the repository level.

questions.explanation: GitHub Actions environment secrets are only exposed to jobs whose workflow explicitly targets that environment via the environment: key, so other workflows in the repository can't read them. Recreating the secret as a repository secret makes it available to every workflow in that repository without requiring each workflow to reference an environment; moving it to the organization level would be unnecessary scope expansion since only one repository needs access. **Learn more:** [Using secrets in GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/using-secrets-in-github-actions)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are automating the build process for a Java-based application using Azure DevOps.  
  
You need to add code coverage testing and publish the results to the pipeline.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
JaCoCo (Java Code Coverage) is the standard code coverage tool for Java applications. It integrates with Maven or Gradle builds to measure code coverage during test execution and generates XML/HTML reports. Azure Pipelines includes the Publish Code Coverage Results task, which natively supports JaCoCo (and Cobertura) report formats, allowing the coverage results to be published and viewed in the pipeline's Code Coverage tab. Bullseye Coverage targets C/C++ code coverage, JUnit is a unit testing framework rather than a coverage tool, and MSTest is a .NET testing framework, none of which are appropriate for Java code coverage reporting in this scenario.

**Learn more:** [PublishCodeCoverageResults@2 - Publish code coverage results v2 task | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/reference/publish-code-coverage-results-v2?view=azure-pipelines) · [Review and configure code coverage results in Azure Pipelines - Azure Pipelines | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/test/review-code-coverage-results?view=azure-devops)

You use Azure Pipelines to manage project builds and deployments.  
  
You plan to use Azure Pipelines for Microsoft Teams to notify the legal team when a new build is ready for release.  
  
You need to configure the Organization Settings in Azure DevOps to support Azure Pipelines for Microsoft Teams.  
  
What should you turn on?

options.text: Azure Active Directory Conditional Access Policy Validation

questions.explanation:
To use the Azure Pipelines app for Microsoft Teams, the Azure DevOps organization must allow third-party applications to authenticate via OAuth. This setting is found under Organization Settings > Security > Policies as "Third-party application access via OAuth," and it must be enabled before the Teams (or Slack) integration app can connect to the organization and post build/release notifications. The other listed policies govern unrelated security features (Conditional Access validation, alternate credentials for legacy authentication, and SSH key authentication) and have no bearing on enabling the Teams notification integration.

**Learn more:** [Azure Pipelines app for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/customize-pipeline/teams) · [About security policies - Azure DevOps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/organizations/security/manage-tokens-policies)

Solution: You use Azure Log Analytics.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Log Analytics is the Azure portal tool for interactively writing, testing, and running Azure Monitor log queries. It uses Kusto Query Language (KQL), which supports ad-hoc analysis of Azure Monitor data, including Application Insights telemetry and Azure SQL monitoring data collected in a Log Analytics workspace.\
\
**Learn more:** [Log queries in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/log-query-overview) · [Overview of Log Analytics in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/log-analytics-overview)

questions.domain: Implement an instrumentation strategy
questions.question:
Solution: You use Transact-SQL.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor Logs and Log Analytics use Kusto Query Language (KQL) to query and analyze monitoring data. Azure SQL Database monitoring data can be analyzed in Azure Monitor Logs with KQL, so Transact-SQL does not satisfy the requirement for ad-hoc monitoring queries.\
\
**Learn more:** [Monitor Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/monitoring-sql-database-azure-monitor?preserve-view=true&view=azuresql-db) · [Overview of Log Analytics in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/log-analytics-overview)

questions.question:
Solution: You use the Contextual Query Language (CQL).  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure monitoring and Application Insights log data are analyzed with Kusto Query Language (KQL). Contextual Query Language (CQL) is not the query language used for these Azure monitoring services, so it does not satisfy the requirement for ad-hoc monitoring queries.\
\
**Learn more:** [Monitor Azure SQL Database - Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/monitoring-sql-database-azure-monitor?preserve-view=true&view=azuresql-db) · [Queries - Kusto](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/kusto/query/queries?view=azure-data-explorer)

questions.question:
Your company has 60 developers who are assigned to four teams. Each team has 15 members.  

The company uses an agile development methodology.  

You need to structure the work of the development teams so that each team owns their respective work while working together to reach a common goal.  

Which parts of the taxonomy should you enable the team to perform autonomously?
questions.explanation: In scaled agile's 'line of autonomy,' development teams work autonomously on user stories and tasks (lower levels of the taxonomy), while management manages epics and features (higher levels) for strategic alignment. This structure balances team independence with organizational cohesion.

questions.question:
Solution: You configure the pipeline definition by using these elements.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785752198125-09yakj0z.png)  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
`trigger` defines a CI trigger, which runs when code is pushed to a branch matching its filters. It does not create a pull-request trigger. Pull-request runs must be configured with `pr` where supported; Azure Repos Git uses a build-validation branch policy for PR validation. Thus, the configuration cannot ensure runs occur only when a PR is created.\
\
**Learn more:** [Triggers in Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/build/triggers?view=azure-devops) · [pr definition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/yaml-schema/pr?view=azure-pipelines)

questions.domain: Implement an instrumentation strategy
questions.question:
Solution: You configure the pipeline definition using the following elements.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785752200457-tdf1n9mp.png)  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
`trigger` configures continuous-integration runs for commits. Its `branches` filter matches branch names, so `pr` is treated as a branch name rather than a pull-request trigger. Pull-request runs must be configured with the `pr` keyword (or, for Azure Repos Git, a build-validation branch policy).\
\
**Learn more:** [Triggers in Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/build/triggers?view=azure-devops) · [pr definition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/yaml-schema/pr?view=azure-pipelines)

Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Pipelines PR triggers support separate `branches` and `paths` include filters. The path filter shown includes `/pr`, rather than the required `/webapp`, so changes to the required folder are not selected. PR triggers also run when a pull request is opened and when it is updated, not only at initial creation. What should you do first?

options.text: Create a conditional access policy in Azure AD.
Create an Azure Active Directory B2C (Azure AD B2C) tenant.
Modify the Security settings of the GitHub organization.

questions.explanation:
To integrate GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) for single sign-on, the first step is to add GitHub from the Azure AD application gallery as an enterprise application (registering GitHub in Azure AD). This registration generates the SAML configuration values (Entra Identifier, Login URL, and signing certificate) that are required later when enabling SAML authentication in the GitHub organization's Security settings. Only after GitHub is registered as an application in Azure AD can the SAML configuration be completed on both the Azure AD side and the GitHub side.

**Learn more:** [Configure a GitHub Enterprise Cloud Organization for Single sign-on with Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/saas-apps/github-tutorial)

questions.question:
Solution: Implement the Test Results Trend widget.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Test Results Trend widget monitors test outcomes over time and identifies patterns in failures, including non-deterministic behavior. This helps isolate intermittent, flaky test failures and reduces troubleshooting effort. [Configure the Test Results Trend (Advanced) widget](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/report/dashboards/configure-test-results-trend?view=azure-devops)\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure the Test Results Trend (Advanced) widget](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/report/dashboards/configure-test-results-trend?view=azure-devops)

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
Solution: Enable flaky test management.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Flaky test management is intended for tests that produce inconsistent pass/fail outcomes without changes to source code or the execution environment. It detects and tracks those tests across pipeline runs, helping isolate and troubleshoot intermittent failures with less effort.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage flaky tests - Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/test/flaky-test-management?view=azure-devops)

questions.domain: Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.question:
Solution: Enable Test Impact Analysis (TIA).  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Test Impact Analysis accelerates pipeline validation by selecting tests affected by a code change. It does not analyze recurring, nondeterministic test failures that are unrelated to code or environment changes; failure-trend analytics is needed to investigate flaky tests.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use Test Impact Analysis - Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/test/test-impact-analysis?view=azure-devops) · [Test Analytics - Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/test/test-analytics?view=azure-devops)

questions.domain: Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.question:
Solution: You increase the code coverage.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Intermittent pass/fail behavior with no changes to source code or the execution environment is a flaky test. Code coverage measures exercised code and does not identify or manage flaky test failures. Azure DevOps flaky-test management supports detecting, marking, and tracking such tests to assist troubleshooting.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage flaky tests - Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/test/flaky-test-management?view=azure-devops)

questions.question:
You need to the merge the POC branch into the default branch. The solution must meet the technical requirements.  

Which command should you run?
questions.explanation: Rebase replaces the default branch's commit history with the POC branch's history, satisfying the requirement that 'the commit history of the POC branch must replace the history of the default branch.' Merge would create a merge commit; --squash collapses commits; --allow-unrelated-histories is for disconnected histories.

You have an Azure DevOps project that contains a build pipeline. The build pipeline uses approximately 50 open source libraries.  

You need to ensure that all the open source libraries comply with your company's licensing standards.  

Which service should you use?
questions.explanation: WhiteSource Bolt is a DevOps plugin for Azure Pipelines that scans open source components and ensures license compliance. It integrates directly into the build pipeline and can block builds if license violations are detected, providing automated compliance verification.

You use WhiteSource Bolt to scan a Node.js application. The scan identifies numerous libraries that have invalid licenses. These libraries are used only during development and are not part of the production deployment.  
  
You need to ensure that WhiteSource Bolt only scans production dependencies.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Run npm install and specify the --production flag.
Modify the WhiteSource Bolt policy and set the action for the licenses used by the development tools to Reassign.
Modify the devDependencies section of the project's Package.json file.
Configure WhiteSource Bolt to scan the node_modules directory only.

questions.explanation:
WhiteSource Bolt scans the node_modules directory that npm install produces. Packages that are only needed for development should be listed in the devDependencies section of package.json rather than dependencies, and running npm install with the --production flag causes npm to skip installing devDependencies. Together, these actions ensure that only production dependencies get installed into node_modules and are therefore scanned by WhiteSource Bolt, eliminating false license violations from development-only tools.

**Learn more:** [npm-install | npm Docs](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/commands/npm-install) · [package.json - devDependencies | npm Docs](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/configuring-npm/package-json#devdependencies)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization runs Jenkins in the cloud for its build pipeline. You need to configure Jenkins so it is able to pull source code from Azure Repos.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the overall solution.  
  
(Choose three.)

options.text: Add the Team Foundation Server (TFS) plug-in to Jenkins.
Add a personal access token to your Jenkins account.
Create a personal access token (PAT) in your Azure DevOps account.
Create a service hook in Azure DevOps.

questions.explanation:
Jenkins does not natively speak the Azure Repos/TFS protocol, so the TFS plug-in must be added to Jenkins to enable it to connect to and check out code from Azure Repos. Because Azure DevOps requires token-based authentication for external tools, a Personal Access Token (PAT) with appropriate (code read) scope must be created in the Azure DevOps organization. That PAT then needs to be added to the Jenkins account/credential store so Jenkins can authenticate to Azure DevOps when retrieving the source. Webhooks and service hooks relate to triggering events (like starting a build on a code push), not to the mechanics of source retrieval, so they are not part of this particular requirement.

**Learn more:** [Jenkins & Azure Repos (AZ-400 notes)](https://github.com/undergroundwires/Azure-in-bullet-points/blob/master/AZ-400%20Microsoft%20Azure%20DevOps%20Solutions/7.3.%20Jenkins.md) · [GitHub - jenkinsci/tfs-plugin: Jenkins tfs plugin](https://github.com/jenkinsci/tfs-plugin)

You have an Azure subscription that contains an app named App1.  
  
You have an Azure DevOps project with two environments named Staging and Production.  
  
You use Azure Pipelines to deploy App1.  
  
You need to validate App1 performance in the Staging environment before deploying it to Production. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do in the Azure DevOps project?

options.text: In the production branch policy, add a status check to query Azure Monitor Alerts for active alerts.
In the Production environment, add a check to query Azure Monitor Alerts for active alerts.
In the Production environment stage, add a post-deployment approval for the Azure Monitor Alerts group.
In the Staging environment add a check to query Azure Monitor Alerts for active alerts.

questions.explanation:
Azure DevOps environment checks must succeed before a stage can consume that environment. A Query Azure Monitor Alerts check on the Production environment automatically blocks the Production deployment when relevant Azure Monitor alerts remain active after the Staging deployment, providing a performance-health gate without manual approvals.

**Learn more:** [Define approvals and checks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/process/approvals?view=azure-devops)

You use Bicep templates to deploy websites and Azure SQL infrastructure.  
  
You need to automate the deployments by using Azure Pipelines and a self-hosted agent that runs on two virtual machines. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: On each virtual machine, enable a system-assigned managed identity.

questions.explanation: For self-hosted agents to authenticate to Azure and deploy resources, a service principal should be created first and configured as a service connection in Azure Pipelines. While managed identities (particularly user-assigned) could theoretically work on Azure VMs, service principals are the officially recommended and most commonly used approach for self-hosted agent authentication to Azure.

You have an Azure subscription that contains an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) instance named AKS1.  
  
You collect and analyze metrics for AKS1 by using the Azure Monitor managed service for Prometheus.  
  
You need to analyze the performance of AKS1.  
  
Which query language should you use?
questions.explanation: PromQL (Prometheus Query Language) is the query language for Prometheus metrics. Azure Monitor's managed service for Prometheus uses PromQL for querying metrics from AKS and other sources. PL/SQL is for Oracle databases, SparkQL is for Spark analytics, and KQL (Kusto Query Language) is used for Log Analytics logs, not metrics.

You need to analyze the agent pool usage.  
  
What are two ways to achieve the goal? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Review the historical graph for the agent pools.

questions.explanation: Agent pool usage can be analyzed through two methods: reviewing the historical graph in Azure Pipelines UI (option A) or querying the TaskAgentPoolSizeSnapshot endpoint via the Analytics API (option C). The Pipeline duration report shows build times, not pool utilization; PipelineRun data shows job execution, not pool allocation patterns.

You need to install the required frameworks to support the planned deployment.

Change the self-hosted agent to use Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 9.

questions.explanation: Container jobs isolate the build environments by running each job in its own container, preventing dependency conflicts between App1 and App2. Each container can have its own dependency configuration, avoiding interference. This approach is more cost-effective than adding additional agents or infrastructure and provides better isolation than Docker Compose tasks alone.

Your company uses GitHub for source control. The company has a team that performs code reviews.  

You need to automate the assignment of the code reviews. The solution must meet the following requirements:  

✑ Prioritize the assignment of code reviews to team members who have the fewest outstanding assignments.  

✑ Ensure that each team member performs an equal number of code reviews in any 30-day period.  

✑ Prevent the assignment of code reviews to the team leader.  

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Clear Never assign certain team members.
Select If assigning team members, don't notify the entire team.
Select Never assign certain team members.
Set Routing algorithm to Round robin.
Set Routing algorithm to Load balance.

questions.explanation: GitHub's load balance routing algorithm ensures reviewers are selected based on recent review request counts and outstanding assignments, distributing reviews equally across team members in any 30-day period. The 'Never assign certain team members' setting excludes the team leader from assignments. Together, these two settings meet all three requirements: equal distribution, prevention of team leader assignment, and prioritization by fewest outstanding reviews.

The Azure Key Vault configuration provider used by ASP.NET Core applications loads secrets by first listing the secrets available in the vault and then retrieving the value of each one, so it requires both the List permission (to enumerate secret names) and the Get permission (to read each secret's value). Granting only one of these permissions would prevent the configuration provider from successfully loading all required configuration values, while granting broader permissions (such as Set, Delete, or Manage) would violate least privilege since the application only needs read access to configuration secrets.

You have a bug work item that has an ID of 123.

questions.explanation: Azure DevOps supports automatic work item state changes via commit message keywords. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company uses ServiceNow for incident management. You are developing an application that runs on Azure. The company requires that a ticket be generated in ServiceNow whenever the application fails to authenticate.  
  
Which Azure Log Analytics solution should you use?
questions.explanation:
The IT Service Management Connector (ITSMC) in Azure Monitor/Log Analytics lets you connect a Log Analytics workspace to an ITSM product such as ServiceNow. After establishing the ITSM connection, you can configure an alert rule (for example, a log search alert that detects authentication failures) to trigger an ITSM action in an action group, which automatically creates a work item (incident, event, or alert) in the connected ServiceNow instance. None of the other listed solutions (Application Insights Connector, Automation & Control, Insight & Analytics) provide this bidirectional integration with an external ITSM/ticketing system.

**Learn more:** [IT Service Management Connector in Log Analytics - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/itsmc-definition) · [Connect ServiceNow with IT Service Management Connector - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/itsmc-connections-servicenow)

You have a 1-TB Azure Repos repository named repo1.  
  
You need to clone repo1. The solution must meet the following requirements:  

• You must be able to search the commit history of the /src directory  

• The amount of time it takes to clone the repository must be minimized  
  
Which command should you run?
questions.explanation: The --filter=blob:none option performs a blobless clone by downloading only commit metadata and directory structures, omitting file contents until needed. This minimizes clone time while preserving full commit history for searching. The --depth-1 option (A) would limit history retrieval and fail the search requirement.

You have a 1-TB Azure Repos repository named repo1.  
  
You need to clone repo1. The solution must meet the following requirements:  

• You must be able to search the commit history of the /src directory  

• The amount of time it takes to clone the repository must be minimized  
  
Which command should you run?
questions.explanation:
A squash merge takes all the individual commits from a source (topic) branch and combines them into one new commit when the pull request is completed into the target branch. This satisfies the requirement to consolidate the commit history and merge the feature's changes as a single commit on master, making the master branch history clean and easy to follow. In contrast, fast-forward and no-fast-forward merges preserve every individual commit from the source branch (the latter also adding a merge commit), so they do not consolidate history into one commit. Git fetch only downloads objects/refs from a remote repository and is not a merge strategy. Azure Repos branch policies allow you to require squash merging for pull requests targeting a protected branch.

**Learn more:** [Improve code quality with branch policies - Azure Repos](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/git/branch-policies) · [Configure branch policies - Require squash merge](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/git/branch-policies?view=azure-devops#require-a-merge-strategy)

options.text: From Azure DevOps, modify the build definition.
From SonarQube, obtain an authentication token.
From Azure DevOps, create a service endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Before Azure DevOps can connect to SonarQube for build/code analysis, an authentication token must exist in SonarQube because it is required as an input when creating the SonarQube service endpoint in Azure DevOps. The correct sequence is to generate the token in SonarQube first (via My Account > Security > Generate Tokens), then use that token to create the service connection in Azure DevOps, and finally update the build definition to include SonarQube analysis tasks referencing that connection. Since the service endpoint cannot be created without the token, obtaining the authentication token from SonarQube is the necessary first step.

**Learn more:** [Setting up project integration | SonarQube Server | Sonar Documentation](https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/devops-platform-integration/azure-devops-integration/setting-up-project-integration) · [Azure DevOps integration | SonarQube Server | Sonar Documentation](https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/10.8/devops-platform-integration/azure-devops-integration)

[if(parameters('isComplete'), '1a', '2a')]  
  
You need to migrate the template to Bicep.  
  
Which expression should you run?
questions.explanation: In Bicep, the ternary conditional operator (condition ? trueValue : falseValue) is the modern equivalent of ARM's if() expression. Visual Studio Codespaces provides cloud-hosted development environments that are accessed entirely through a web browser, making them usable from browsers, tablets, and Chromebooks without needing a locally installed IDE. Because the environment lives in the cloud rather than on a specific machine, it naturally supports remote workers and hot-desking, since developers can connect from any device and pick up where they left off. It integrates directly with GitHub repositories and offers a full-featured, integrated debugging experience similar to Visual Studio Code. VS Code, Xamarin Studio, and MonoDevelop are traditional locally installed IDEs that require a compatible desktop OS, so they cannot run on tablets or Chromebooks and don't inherently support hot-desking across arbitrary devices.

**Learn more:** [What is Visual Studio Codespaces?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/codespaces/overview/what-is-vsonline)
